t: What is splittable land in Bali?
s: Whether a parcel can be legally divided decides your exit options, your financing and often the price. Most buyers never ask.
b:
If you are buying land in Bali rather than a finished villa, this is a question that belongs in your first conversation with the notary, and it almost never comes up until much later.

   What it means

A parcel of land in Indonesia is registered at the land office as a single certificate covering a defined area. Splitting it —  pemecahan sertifikat  — means applying to divide that certificate into two or more smaller certificates, each independently transferable.

Land that can be split is worth more than land that cannot, because it can be sold in pieces, developed in phases, or partly released to fund the rest. Land that cannot be split is a single indivisible asset with a single buyer pool.

   What decides whether a parcel can be split

  Minimum plot size for the zone.   Each zone under the regional spatial plan carries a minimum parcel size. Split the land below it and the resulting certificates cannot be issued. In practice this is the constraint that bites most often.

  Road access for every resulting parcel.   Each new certificate needs legal access. A parcel that would be landlocked after division will not be approved, which means a split usually requires giving up a strip of land to an access road, reducing your usable area.

  Zoning consistency.   If the parcel straddles two zones, the division has to respect the boundary, which can force an awkward shape.

  The title type.   Hak Milik parcels split relatively straightforwardly. HGB and Hak Pakai splits are more involved and depend on the terms of the original grant.

  Whether it is already encumbered.   A parcel under an existing lease, mortgage or dispute will not be divided until that is resolved.

   Why it matters to a foreign buyer

You cannot hold Hak Milik, so at first glance this looks like a domestic problem. It is not, for three reasons.

  Your exit.   If you take a thirty year lease over five are and want to sell in year twelve, a buyer who could take two are of it is a much easier sale

t: How bad are Bali's water and waste problems?
s: Groundwater depletion and waste management are the island's real constraints, and both are becoming regulatory risks for property owners.
b:
Bali's environmental pressures are real, they affect property values and rental income directly, and they are moving in one direction.

   Water

The island's water situation is under genuine strain from tourism, agriculture and development competing for a finite supply.

  Groundwater extraction is regulated and requires a permit  , and enforcement has increased as depletion has become a recognised issue. A property drawing from an unpermitted bore is carrying a compliance risk that grows rather than shrinks.

  The Bukit is the acute case.   Limestone geology means deep groundwater, expensive and uncertain boreholes and inconsistent mains supply. A large number of Bukit villas run on   trucked water  , which is a real recurring cost and a genuine operational risk when every villa on the peninsula needs water simultaneously in August.

  The traditional subak irrigation system   — the cooperative water management that shapes Bali's rice terraces and is UNESCO recognised — depends on water that development upstream increasingly diverts. That is a cultural and agricultural issue and also a practical one, because it affects the landscape that the tourism economy is selling.

For a buyer, the practical question is specific:   where does this property's water come from, what does it cost annually, is the extraction permitted, and what happens in peak season?   Get it in writing.

   Waste

Bali's waste infrastructure has not kept pace with visitor numbers and consumption.

Landfill capacity is constrained, collection is inconsistent outside the main areas, and the wet season brings visible accumulation on beaches as rivers carry waste to the coast. This is worst between roughly December and March and it appears in guest reviews.

There are genuine initiatives — beach cleanups, waste banks, plastic reduction regulation — and they have had real effects. The scale of the problem remains larger than the response.

For an owner, two consequences.   Guest experience   is affe

t: Is Pecatu or Ungasan better value than Uluwatu?
s: The interior Bukit, minutes from the famous breaks, at a fraction of clifftop prices. The trade is the view and the water.
b:
The Bukit's clifftop positions are among the most expensive land in Bali. Pecatu and Ungasan sit a few minutes inland from them at a fraction of the price, and for a lot of buyers that is the better trade.

   What they are

  Pecatu   covers the interior of the peninsula behind Uluwatu, including the golf course development and a spread of residential land running toward Padang Padang and Bingin. Limestone, scrub, and increasingly villa clusters.

  Ungasan   sits to the east, above Melasti and Karma beaches, with the same interior character and a run of large resorts along the southern cliffs.

Both are five to fifteen minutes from the famous breaks and beaches, and both are essentially car dependent. There is no walkable strip here in the Canggu sense, though small clusters of cafes and warungs have grown up along the main roads.

   The market

Land is substantially cheaper than clifftop Uluwatu or Bingin, and there is considerably more of it. The Bukit's interior is the largest supply of genuinely developable land remaining in south Bali.

Plot sizes are generous by south Bali standards. That matters for what you can build: a large plot with a KDB coverage limit still leaves room for a proper pool, garden and privacy, which on a tight Canggu plot it does not.

Lease terms are longer at a given budget than anywhere in the Canggu corridor. Building here is a genuine option rather than a theoretical one.

   Rental performance

Good and improving, with a distinct guest profile.

Surf travellers drive a large share of it, and their season follows swell rather than school holidays, which means they fill different weeks than the Australian family market. Repeat and direct booking rates in Bukit surf properties are unusually high.

The family market at Ungasan and Pecatu has grown substantially, drawn by larger villas, quieter surroundings and proximity to the southern beaches.

What you do not get is the nomad long stay demand that fills Canggu's quiet months, becaus

t: What is SKTT and do you need a domicile letter?
s: Getting the KITAS is not the end of the process. Local registration is a separate step and people only discover it when something else is blocked.
b:
The SKTT is one of those documents nobody mentions until you need it, and then you need it for several unrelated things at once.

   What it is

  SKTT   —  Surat Keterangan Tempat Tinggal  — is a certificate of residence issued to a foreign national holding a KITAS, by the local civil registry office (Dukcapil) in the area where you live.

It records that you reside at a specific address in a specific district. It is issued after your stay permit, as part of the post arrival reporting obligations that accompany a KITAS.

   Why it matters

  It is part of your immigration compliance.   Post arrival registration is an obligation, not an optional step, and failing to complete it is a defect in your position that surfaces at extension.

  Banks ask for it.   Opening an Indonesian bank account as a foreign resident frequently requires proof of address, and the SKTT is the document that satisfies it.

  Tax registration.   An NPWP registration as a resident taxpayer requires address documentation, and mismatched or missing address evidence is a common cause of a rejected application under the strict data matching Coretax applies.

  Driving licence.   Obtaining an Indonesian SIM as a foreign resident generally requires proof of residence.

  Schools, utilities, some contracts.   Anywhere that needs to establish you live where you say you do.

  KITAP applications  , which require a documented residential history.

   The related documents

  SKTT   is for KITAS holders, issued by the civil registry.

  SKPPS   or equivalent certificates exist for other permit categories.

  KITAP holders   may obtain a   KTP for foreigners   — an identity card equivalent — which serves a similar function with a longer validity.

  Police reporting (STM)   is a separate registration with the police, and whether it applies depends on the area and the current practice.

Terminology and practice vary by regency and change, so confirm what your specific area requires rather than assuming.

t: What is moving to Bali actually like?
s: The first three months are the holiday. Months four to twelve are the ones that decide whether you stay.
b:
Most of what goes wrong for people moving to Bali is a gap between an expectation formed on holiday and what living here is actually like. The gap is predictable.

   What holidays do not show you

  Traffic  , because on holiday you are not commuting. Journeys a map says take twenty minutes take an hour at peak, and it is worsening.

  The wet season  , if you visited in July. December to March is genuinely different — heavy rain, humidity, mould, flooded streets, waste on the beaches, and fewer people around.

  Administration.   Visas, permits, reporting, tax, bank accounts, driving licences, utilities. Everything takes longer than you expect and is rarely completed in one visit.

  The cost of doing things properly.   Legal residency, tax compliance, insurance, healthcare cover, proper staff arrangements. Living here lawfully costs meaningfully more than living here casually, and the difference is what people underestimate.

  Healthcare.   Good private facilities exist in the south. Serious cases are evacuated to Singapore or Australia, and   medical evacuation insurance is not optional  . Check what your policy actually covers and what it excludes, particularly motorcycle accidents.

  The transience.   The foreign community turns over constantly. People you become close to leave. That is a real and frequently unanticipated part of the experience.

   What is genuinely good

Cost of living is lower than Australia, Western Europe or North America, materially so if you live somewhat locally rather than entirely in the foreign economy.

The climate, the landscape, the ocean.

A large, genuinely entrepreneurial and creative foreign community, particularly around Canggu and Ubud, which is unusual and is a real asset if that is your world.

Domestic help, childcare and services are affordable in a way they are not at home, which changes daily life substantially for families.

Indonesian culture and Balinese community life, which is extraordinary and which you will e

t: How long does it take to build a villa in Bali?
s: Six to twelve months of construction, eighteen to twenty-four from land to first guest, and the pauses are not the contractor's fault.
b:
Almost every Bali build overruns, and the reasons are predictable enough that a realistic programme is possible if you build them in from the start.

   The realistic sequence

  Land search and due diligence: one to three months.   Finding the parcel, then one to three weeks of verification on a clean title, longer where there is an undivided inheritance, an encumbrance or a records discrepancy.

  Design: two to four months.   Concept, developed design, technical drawings and structural calculations. Rushing this is how you get a building that costs more to construct and earns less.

  Permits: variable, and the most unpredictable step.   PBG processing depends on the regency and on how complete the submission is. An incomplete application is returned rather than processed, which is why the design stage matters.

  Construction: six to twelve months   for a straightforward villa once permits are in hand.

  Furniture and fit out: four to eight weeks  , and it can run in parallel with the end of construction if you order early.

  SLF and licensing: weeks  , after completion and inspection.

  Listing, photography and ramp up: six to twelve months   to reach sustainable occupancy, because platform ranking rewards booking history and review volume.

  Land purchase to first guest: eighteen to twenty four months   is realistic. Land purchase to a property performing at its steady state is closer to two and a half to three years.

Model your returns on that, not on construction finishing.

   The pauses to build in

  Nyepi   stops everything island wide for a day — no vehicles, no work, nobody leaving their property.

  Galungan and Kuningan  , the major celebrations ten days apart, pause work and staff have genuine obligations.

  Odalan  , temple anniversary ceremonies on a 210 day cycle, pause work locally and can close roads.

  Cremation ceremonies  , which involve significant community participation.

  The wet season  , roughly November to March, slows groundw

t: Where should you buy around Ubud?
s: Central Ubud is congested and built out. The value and the views are in the villages around it, and each one behaves differently.
b:
Ubud is a market with a different guest, a different booking channel and a different calendar from coastal Bali. It is also, in its centre, congested and effectively built out. The opportunity is in the villages around it.

   Penestanan

A ridge immediately west of central Ubud, reached by a famous set of steps and a road around. Rice fields, artists' studios, a long established foreign community, and a walkable set of cafes and yoga studios.

  Why it works.   Close enough to Ubud centre to walk or ride in minutes, far enough to be quiet. The walkability is genuine, which in Bali is scarce. The community is established rather than transient.

  What it costs.   Land is among the more expensive around Ubud, and plots are often small and awkwardly shaped because of the terrain and the existing development pattern.

  Guest profile.   Long stay Europeans, yoga and wellness visitors, creatives. Longer average stays than the coast and less price sensitivity at the top end.

   Sayan and the Ayung valley

West of Penestanan, where the land falls away into the Ayung river gorge.

  Why it works.   The valley views are the best in the Ubud area and among the best in Bali. Several of the island's most prestigious resorts are here, which anchors the location's reputation and the price.

  What it costs.   The most expensive land around Ubud, and rightly so. Valley edge parcels with a protected outlook are genuinely scarce.

  What to check.   Slope stability and the cost of building on it. Retaining and foundations on a gorge edge plot are a large part of the budget. And river setback — the sempadan sungai applies and is strictly enforced.

   Tegallalang

North of Ubud, known for the rice terraces and now a long strip of swings, cafes and viewpoints along the main road.

  Why it works.   Land is considerably cheaper than Penestanan or Sayan, plots are larger, and the rice terrace views are real. There is genuine development land.

  What it costs you.   Fifteen to thirty

t: Nusa Penida or Lembongan?
s: Penida is bigger, rawer and cheaper with a day-trip economy. Lembongan is smaller, more developed and has actual overnight demand.
b:
The three Nusa islands get grouped together and they are genuinely different propositions. The choice between the two largest turns on one thing: whether visitors stay the night.

   Nusa Penida

  The largest by a wide margin  , rugged, with dramatic limestone cliffs, Kelingking, Broken Beach and Angel's Billabong, and a permanent population many times Lembongan's.

  Visitor numbers are enormous   and the overwhelming majority arrive on a fast boat in the morning, tour the famous viewpoints by car, and leave in the afternoon.

That day trip pattern is the defining commercial fact.   Enormous visitor numbers produce very little accommodation demand.  

  Infrastructure is genuinely limited.   Roads across the island are poor and in places difficult, water is scarce, power is less robust than Lembongan's, and medical facilities are minimal.

  Land is the cheapest of the three islands  , with dramatic clifftop positions unobtainable at the price anywhere in Bali.

   Nusa Lembongan

  Small, and the most developed   of the three, with Mushroom Bay, Jungutbatu and the village as established centres.

  Overnight demand is real.   Lembongan made the transition from a day trip destination to one where people stay several nights, and that shift is what makes accommodation viable there and not on Penida.

  Diving and snorkelling   — manta rays, drift dives, clear water — is world class and is the basis of the demand.

  Infrastructure is better than Penida's  , which is a low bar, and still constrained: water is limited and depends on shipping, trucking or desalination, and power is less robust than the mainland.

  Land is more expensive than Penida's   and far cheaper than Bali's.

   The commercial comparison

  Lembongan has a rental market. Penida largely does not.  

That is the whole thing. A well presented small property on Lembongan with a view and easy beach access can perform. The equivalent on Penida is competing for a guest who is not staying the night.

t: When do you need a sworn translation?
s: Foreign documents generally need legalisation and a sworn translation before Indonesian offices will accept them, and the chain takes weeks.
b:
Every operative document in an Indonesian property transaction is in Bahasa Indonesia, and the Indonesian version governs. A sworn translation is how you know what you are signing.

   What a sworn translation is

A translation produced by a   penerjemah tersumpah   — a sworn translator formally appointed and authorised to produce translations that carry legal weight.

It is not the same as a good translation. A fluent bilingual friend, an agent, or a translation app can tell you what a document says. None of those produce a document that an Indonesian authority, a court, an embassy or a notary will accept as an authoritative rendering.

The distinction matters at exactly the moments it is expensive to discover.

   When you need one

  Property documents you are signing.   A lease deed, a sale and purchase deed, a power of attorney. You are committing to a contract in a language you probably do not read, and the Indonesian version is the one that governs regardless of any English summary.

  Foreign documents submitted to Indonesian authorities.   Birth certificates, marriage certificates, police clearances, academic qualifications, company documents — for visa applications, company formation, marriage registration, or land office matters.

  Indonesian documents submitted abroad.   Certificates, deeds, company documents, court records.

  Anything going to court.  

   The chain for foreign documents

A foreign document usually needs more than translation before an Indonesian authority will accept it.

The sequence is typically: the document is   notarised or certified   in its country of origin, then   legalised   — either by apostille where both countries are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention, which now includes Indonesia, or through consular legalisation where they are not — and then   translated by a sworn translator  .

Order matters. Translating first and legalising afterwards frequently means doing it twice. Ask the receiving authority what sequence

t: Is Bali running out of flight capacity?
s: Ngurah Rai is the constraint on arrivals, which makes it the constraint on rental demand. More villas do not create more visitors.
b:
Bali's rental market is a function of how many seats arrive. That is the constraint underneath every occupancy projection and it is almost never in one.

   Why it matters more than anything else

Bali has   one international airport  . Ngurah Rai is the single gateway for essentially all foreign arrivals, and it has finite capacity in terminal throughput, runway slots and ground handling.

Every guest in your villa arrived through it. If seat capacity into Denpasar falls, occupancy falls across the entire island regardless of how good your property is, how sharp your pricing is or how well your manager performs.

No amount of operational quality compensates for seats that do not exist.

   Where the seats come from

  Australia   is the largest and most consistent source of capacity, with high frequency services from Perth, Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane across full service and low cost carriers. Australian capacity is the backbone of the Bali market.

  Domestic Indonesian   traffic from Jakarta, Surabaya and elsewhere is very large in volume, though it feeds a different segment from the foreign villa market.

  Asian regional   — Singapore, Malaysia, Korea, Japan, China, India — is the fastest moving component and the most sensitive to policy, currency and sentiment.

  Europe   is thinner, largely one stop via Middle East and Asian hubs, with a small number of direct services. European guests stay longer, which partly offsets the lower seat count.

   What moves capacity

  Airline route decisions  , made on profitability across a network, with Bali competing against every other destination an airline could deploy an aircraft to.

  Aircraft availability  , which has been constrained globally.

  Fuel and currency.  

  Policy   — visa arrangements, entry requirements, bilateral agreements.

t: What documents do you need to buy property in Bali?
s: The list is short, and the ones that matter most are the documents the seller has to produce, not the ones you do.
b:
Buyers arrive expecting a large paperwork burden on their side. In practice what you need to supply is minimal. The serious document work is on the seller's side, and it is where transactions fail.

   What you need to provide

  Passport.   Valid, with reasonable time remaining. This is the core identity document for a foreign buyer.

  A visa or stay permit  , depending on the route. For a straightforward leasehold, a tourist visa is sufficient — you can sign a lease on a visa on arrival. For   Hak Pakai   you need a KITAS or KITAP, because the title is only available to holders of residency. For a purchase through a   PT PMA  , the company is the buyer and the company documents carry the transaction.

  NPWP  , an Indonesian tax number, is required for titled transactions and for anything the tax office needs to see. Since 2024 the NPWP has been integrated with the national identity numbering, and Coretax now requires the linked identifier for filings. If you are buying through a company or taking a registered title, get this arranged early rather than at signing.

  An Indonesian bank account  , if you intend to pay domestically or receive rental income. Not strictly required to buy, and much easier to open once you hold a KITAS.

  A prenuptial or postnuptial agreement  , if you are married to an Indonesian citizen and intend to take a registered title in your own name. Without one, Indonesian marital property rules treat assets as jointly held, which collides with the rule that a foreigner cannot hold Hak Milik. This catches people, and it is not fixable retroactively without difficulty.

   What the seller must produce

This is the part that decides whether the deal is real.

  The original land certificate.   Not a photocopy, not a photograph. The original, inspected by your notary, with the details checked against the land office record.

  Proof of the seller's identity and authority.   The name on the certificate must match the person selling. If it does

t: Is East Bali coast worth buying?
s: Black sand, world-class diving and prices a fraction of the south. Rental demand is thin and seasonal, and that is the whole trade.
b:
The east coast around Amed and Candidasa is Bali's diving coast, and it is priced at a fraction of the south for reasons that are entirely rational.

   What it is

  Amed   is a string of small fishing villages along a dry, dramatic stretch of coast in the far east, below Mount Agung. Black sand and pebble beaches, traditional salt production, and the calm water of the Lombok Strait.

The   USAT Liberty wreck at Tulamben  , a short distance north, is one of the most dived sites in Indonesia and is accessible directly from shore. That single feature underpins much of the area's visitor economy.

  Candidasa   sits further southwest, a slightly more developed resort strip that has been quiet since coastal erosion damaged its beach decades ago, with breakwaters now in place.

Both are in   Karangasem regency  , and both are roughly two to two and a half hours from the airport.

   The market

  Land is very cheap   by southern standards, with coastal and elevated positions available at a fraction of Canggu or the Bukit. Plots are large and lease terms available are long.

Existing stock is small hotels, dive resorts and guesthouses rather than villa product of the kind foreign buyers usually look for. This is a land and build market.

   Rental performance

  Thin, seasonal and specific.  

The guest is a diver or a snorkeller. That is the core of the demand and it is a genuinely loyal market — divers return to sites they like, they book direct, and they stay several nights.

Beyond diving there is a small quiet seeking market, and traffic from people on multi day Bali itineraries.

What is absent: any nomad market, any meaningful long stay foreign resident base, any walkable amenity of the Canggu type, and any year round demand floor. The quiet months are genuinely quiet.

Occupancy that would be a failure in the south is normal here. A well presented property with a sea view and easy dive access can hold decent rates because quality supply is limited, but filling th

t: Should you list a Bali villa exclusively or with every agent?
s: Open listings feel safer and usually sell for less. The reason is what an agent will and will not spend money on.
b:
Sellers in Bali overwhelmingly choose open listings — giving the property to six or eight agents at once — on the theory that more agents means more buyers. The outcome is usually the opposite, and the mechanism is worth understanding before you decide.

   What each one means

  Open listing.   Any agent may market the property. Whoever brings the buyer earns the commission. No agent has any protected position.

  Exclusive listing.   One agency markets the property for a defined period, commonly three to six months, and earns the commission on any sale in that window regardless of who introduces the buyer.

There is no licensing regime for real estate agents in Indonesia, so neither arrangement carries the professional obligations it would in Australia or the UK. Whatever protection you have comes from the contract you sign, and nothing else.

   Why open listings underperform

An agent's marketing budget goes where the return is predictable.

On an open listing, an agent who spends USD 800 on photography, drone footage, a video walkthrough and paid placement has a meaningful chance of another agency closing the buyer those assets attracted. The rational response is to spend nothing: put it on the website with the owner's phone photos, and wait for an enquiry that happens to land.

That is exactly what happens. Look at almost any open listed Bali villa and you will find four agencies carrying the same six mediocre photographs.

Meanwhile the property appears at four slightly different prices, because each agency adds its own margin or negotiates independently. A buyer who sees the same villa at USD 340,000, USD 355,000 and USD 365,000 concludes the seller is not serious, and opens at USD 300,000.

The third effect is that nobody owns the sale. No agent qualifies buyers properly, follows up, or manages the negotiation, because the effort might benefit a competitor.

   What an exclusive buys you

A budget. An agent with a protected position will commission proper p

t: How do you plan an exit from Bali property?
s: Your buyer pool is decided on the day you purchase, not the day you list. Almost nobody models this and it is where returns are actually realised.
b:
A return is not realised until the money is back. In Bali, getting it back is the hardest part of the transaction and the part nobody models.

   Your buyer pool is set at purchase

The day you buy, you determine who can buy it from you.

A   USD 250,000 three bedroom in Pererenan on a long lease   has hundreds of plausible buyers at any moment. It is the most traded product in Bali.

A   USD 900,000 five bedroom   has perhaps a dozen, and they are not all looking this year.

A   USD 400,000 villa with eleven years remaining   has almost nobody, because the arithmetic only works at a price the seller will not accept.

A   property with no PBG, or in a zone that does not permit letting  , is unsaleable to anyone doing due diligence, which means it is saleable only to someone who is not.

None of that changes between purchase and sale. It is fixed on day one, and it is the single most predictable thing about your eventual exit.

   How long it actually takes

Under USD 500,000 with a long term in a good area: three to nine months.

USD 500,000 to USD 750,000: six to eighteen months.

Above USD 750,000: twelve to twenty four months, frequently at a discount to asking.

On a leasehold, the term runs down for every month of that. A villa that takes eighteen months to sell is a villa that lost eighteen months of term while it sat, which compresses the price further. The wait is not neutral; it is a cost that compounds.

   The four exits

  Sell the remaining lease.   The normal route. Requires the deed to permit assignment, and where landowner consent is needed, that consent has a price set at the moment you have a buyer waiting. Sort this out before you list, not during.

  Sell the company.   If the property is held in a PT PMA, you can sell the shares rather than the asset. That can be cleaner and faster for the right buyer, and it narrows the pool to buyers willing to take on an Indonesian company with its history and liabilities. Get the accounts clean well in advan

t: How do you build a sustainable villa in Bali?
s: Most of what reduces environmental impact here also reduces your running costs. The rest is expensive signalling.
b:
Sustainability in Bali villas ranges from genuinely useful engineering to bamboo and bare concrete signalling. The useful version is mostly indistinguishable from good design for the climate, and it cuts your operating costs.

   Start with design, not equipment

The largest environmental cost of a Bali villa is   cooling  , and the cheapest way to reduce it is to design a building that needs less of it.

  Cross ventilation.   Openings that let air move through rather than into a room.

  Deep overhangs.   Keep sun off walls and glass and rain off everything. This single decision affects cooling load, maintenance and comfort more than any product you can buy.

  Orientation   away from the worst afternoon sun, with west facing glass shaded.

  Roof insulation  , frequently omitted in Bali builds and one of the highest return specifications available. An uninsulated roof turns the building into a heat store that aircon fights all night.

  High ceilings and shade  , which is what traditional Balinese architecture did before anyone called it sustainable.

None of that costs meaningfully more than building badly, and all of it reduces your electricity bill permanently.

   Water, which is the real constraint

Bali's water is under genuine strain from tourism, agriculture and development.

  Groundwater extraction is regulated and requires a permit  , and enforcement has increased. A property drawing from an unpermitted bore carries a compliance risk that grows.

  Rainwater harvesting   is straightforward here given the rainfall, and it reduces both cost and draw.

  Greywater separation   — sink, shower and laundry water routed to irrigation rather than the septic system — reduces load, reduces cost and keeps the garden alive.

  A pool cover   cuts evaporation meaningfully in this climate and reduces chemical use. Underused in Bali.

  Efficient fittings  , which cost little.

  Proper wastewater treatment   rather than the cheapest compliant tank. Most of Bali has

t: Can you study in Indonesia on a student visa?
s: Sponsored by the institution, not by you, and it does not permit work. The language-school route is the one foreigners in Bali actually use.
b:
The student route is a legitimate residency path that is less used by foreigners in Bali than it could be, partly because people do not realise what qualifies.

   What it is

A stay permit sponsored by an   accredited Indonesian educational institution   for the duration of a course of study.

It covers formal education — universities, schools, and accredited language and vocational programmes — and depends entirely on the institution being recognised and willing to sponsor.

   Who actually uses it

  Degree students   at Indonesian universities, including at Udayana in Bali.

  Language students   on serious Bahasa Indonesia programmes at accredited institutions. This is the route most relevant to adults who want to be here legitimately while learning the language.

  Research students   and those on exchange arrangements.

  Vocational and arts students   — traditional music, dance, crafts — at recognised institutions, which is a genuine and underused category in Bali specifically.

  Children of foreign residents   attending Indonesian schools, although dependants of a KITAS holder are usually covered through a family permit instead.

   What it requires

  An accredited sponsoring institution   willing to act. This is the first and hardest step, and not every institution advertising courses to foreigners is in a position to sponsor a permit.

  Acceptance onto a course  , with documentation.

  Ministry approval   through the education pathway in addition to the immigration process.

  Financial evidence   and accommodation documentation.

  Post arrival reporting  , including registration and an SKTT.

The process is slower than most permit routes because it runs through two ministries rather than one. Allow considerably more time than you expect.

   What it does not permit

  Work.   A student permit authorises study. Employment, freelancing for Indonesian clients, or running a business operationally all require separate authorisation.

This catches people

t: Spain or Bali for property?
s: Spain gives registered EU freehold and ended its golden visa. Bali gives higher yield and no ownership. The wealth tax is the wildcard.
b:
Spain and Bali attract overlapping buyers — sun, coast, a lower cost of living than northern Europe — and they differ on almost everything that matters commercially.

   Ownership

  Spain.   Full registered freehold in your own name, no restriction on foreign buyers, EU property law, a functioning land registry, and mortgages available to non residents.

  Bali.   No freehold for foreigners. Leasehold by contract, unregistered and unmortgageable, or Hak Pakai with residency, or HGB through a company.

Not a close comparison. Spain is an ordinary European property market.

   The golden visa

  Spain ended its golden visa programme.   The property linked residency route that drew a substantial share of non EU buying is closed.

  Indonesia's second home and golden visa routes   exist, are newer with administrative practice still settling, and are generally based on funds, investment or qualifications rather than straightforwardly on buying property.

Neither country now offers residency for buying a house. Anyone told otherwise about either is working from old information.

   The wealth tax, which is Spain's distinguishing feature

  Spain levies a wealth tax  , administered regionally with substantial variation between autonomous communities, alongside a national level solidarity levy on large fortunes.

That taxes the   value of what you own annually  , regardless of the income it produces — which is a materially different proposition from a tax on rental profit.

  Indonesia has no wealth tax.   It taxes rental income and the transfer value on disposal, plus a modest annual land and building tax.

For someone with assets rather than high income, this is the largest single difference between the two, and it is the reason a meaningful amount of European capital looks east.

The caveat that applies everywhere:   your home jurisdiction follows the asset.   If you remain tax resident in a jurisdiction taxing worldwide wealth, holding property in Indonesia does not re

t: What health insurance do you need in Bali?
s: Good private care exists in the south, and serious cases leave the island. Evacuation cover is the difference between an inconvenience and a catastrophe.
b:
Bali has decent private hospitals and a hard ceiling on what they can handle. Understanding where that ceiling sits is what determines the cover you need.

   What is available locally

  Private hospitals in the south   — Denpasar, Kuta, Nusa Dua — handle routine and moderately serious care competently. Consultations, imaging, minor surgery, maternity, and most of what a family needs day to day.

  BIMC and Siloam   are the names most foreign residents use, with international standard facilities and English speaking staff.

  Outside the south  , facilities thin rapidly. The east, north, highlands and islands have limited capacity, and serious cases travel.

  BPJS Kesehatan  , the national health insurance, covers residents and is mandatory for employees. It provides genuine coverage within the public system and is not what most foreign residents rely on for serious care.

   Where the ceiling is

  Major trauma, complex cardiac, serious neurological cases, advanced oncology and anything requiring specialist intensive care   generally get evacuated — to Singapore, or to Australia.

That is not a criticism of Bali's hospitals. It is the reality of an island with a finite specialist base, and the medical staff will tell you the same thing.

  Medical evacuation to Singapore costs tens of thousands of dollars and can exceed that substantially.   An air ambulance with a medical team is an expensive aircraft.

This is the single most important number in this article. It is why evacuation cover is not optional.

   What to look for in a policy

  Medical evacuation and repatriation  , with a stated limit that is realistic. A policy with a low evacuation sub limit is a policy that covers part of the flight.

  Inpatient and outpatient cover   at the facilities you would actually use.

  Direct billing arrangements   with local hospitals, so you are not paying tens of thousands up front and claiming afterwards.

  Pre existing condition treatment  , which varies enormousl

t: How do you send money out of Indonesia?
s: Transfers out attract more scrutiny than transfers in. The constraint is documentation rather than permission, and planning it saves both time and spread.
b:
Getting money into Indonesia is straightforward. Getting it out requires documentation, and the people who struggle are the ones who did not keep records as they went.

   The general position

Indonesia does not operate blanket exchange controls preventing repatriation. You can send money out.

What applies is   documentation and reporting  . Banks ask about source and purpose, thresholds trigger reporting, and larger transfers attract more questions.

The constraint is not permission. It is being able to evidence where the money came from.

   What banks will ask

  Source of funds.   Where did this money come from? Rental income, a property sale, your own funds transferred in previously, a company distribution.

  Purpose.   What is the transfer for?

  Supporting documents.   Depending on the amount and the source: the lease or sale deed, rental statements, tax filings, the company's resolution and accounts, or evidence of the original inward transfer.

  Tax evidence  , increasingly. That the Indonesian tax on the income has been dealt with.

Banks vary in how much they ask for, and the same bank varies by branch and by amount. Confirm requirements before initiating a large transfer rather than at the counter.

   The documentation you should have been keeping

This is the practical advice and it is retrospective for most people.

  Evidence of money coming in.   The original transfer confirmations when you funded the purchase. This establishes that funds leaving are your own capital returning rather than untaxed income.

  The lease or purchase deed  , and the sale deed on exit.

  Rental records   — booking data, platform statements, bank credits — matched to your tax filings.

  Tax filings and payment evidence  , both the national final tax and the regional accommodation tax.

  Company records  , if a PT PMA is involved: accounts, tax returns, and the resolution authorising any distribution.

An owner who has this can transfer without difficulty. One who h

t: Is Echo Beach a good place to buy?
s: The northern end of Canggu, surf-led rather than cafe-led, slightly cheaper and with a different guest entirely.
b:
Echo Beach — Pantai Batu Mejan — is where Canggu stops being about cafes and starts being about waves. It sits at the northern end of the strip, just before the Pererenan river mouth.

   What Echo Beach is

A black sand beach with a consistent reef bottom wave that is more serious than Batu Bolong's, a row of beachfront restaurants and bars facing the break, and residential land running back inland.

The atmosphere is different from Batu Bolong a kilometre south. Less dense, less relentless, more surf oriented. The crowd skews toward people who came for the wave rather than the coworking.

It is walkable in a limited sense — the beachfront strip itself is — but the surrounding residential areas are a scooter ride from most things.

   The market

Land here is cheaper than Batu Bolong and Berawa, and there is more of it, particularly as you move back from the beach and toward the river.

Stock is a mix of older properties on generous plots, newer villa developments, and some beachfront commercial. Plot sizes inland are better than central Canggu, which matters for delivering a proper pool within the KDB limit.

Lease terms at a given budget run longer than the Canggu core, frequently by five to ten years, which is the main commercial argument for the area.

   Rental performance

Good, with a surf weighted guest profile.

Surf travellers book around swell rather than school holidays, which means Echo Beach fills some weeks that the rest of Canggu does not. Repeat rates are high and direct booking is more common than in the cafe driven areas.

There is also solid family and group demand, drawn by larger properties and lower density than Berawa.

Nomad long stay demand exists but is thinner than Batu Bolong's, because the working infrastructure is concentrated further south. The quiet months are correspondingly quieter.

Properties that perform are three and four bedrooms with proper pools and outdoor space, and anything with a genuine view of the break. Small units c

t: How does a multiple entry visa work?
s: Two different numbers govern it, and confusing them is how people overstay without ever intending to.
b:
If you come to Indonesia several times a year, the multiple entry visa is the permit that fits, and it is consistently overlooked by people repeatedly buying visas on arrival.

   What it is

A   visit visa valid for an extended period   — commonly one, two or five years depending on the type — permitting   multiple entries   during that validity, with each individual stay limited to a defined number of days.

The critical distinction: the visa's validity is not the length of any single stay. A visa valid for five years with a sixty day per entry limit does not let you stay for five years. It lets you enter repeatedly, for up to sixty days each time, across five years.

   The categories

  Tourism.   For repeated leisure visits.

  Business.   For meetings, negotiations, site visits, conferences and exhibitions — the same scope as a single entry business visit visa, with repeated entries.

  Family visit.   For visiting family in Indonesia.

Requirements vary by category and typically include a sponsor or guarantor in Indonesia, financial evidence, and supporting documentation explaining the purpose.

   Who it suits

  Property owners who visit several times a year.   This is the obvious case and it is underused. Someone who comes four times a year for two or three weeks is a much better fit for a multiple entry visa than for four separate visas on arrival, and it removes the recurring extension anxiety.

  People doing business across the region   who pass through Indonesia repeatedly.

  Anyone with family here   visiting regularly.

  People who buy a visa on arrival every few months.   Repeated consecutive VOA use attracts attention, and immigration officers can and do decline entry to people who appear to be living in Indonesia on consecutive tourist visas. A multiple entry visa is the correct instrument for genuine repeat visiting and removes that friction.

   What it does not do

  It does not permit work.   It is a visit visa. Meetings and inspections yes

t: Do you need a quantity surveyor in Bali?
s: Someone independent has to price the work, check what was built and verify what you pay for. Without that, the contractor is marking their own homework.
b:
On a Bali build, the money leaves in variations and in payments made against work nobody independently verified. A quantity surveyor or project manager is how you stop both.

   What each role does

  A quantity surveyor   prices the work from the drawings and specification, produces a bill of quantities, evaluates tenders on a like for like basis, values work completed for payment, and prices variations.

  A project manager   runs the programme, coordinates the trades and consultants, inspects work, certifies payments and manages the contractor relationship day to day.

  An architect with supervision in scope   covers part of both — checking that what is built matches the design — without necessarily doing the commercial side.

On a small build one person may cover it. Above roughly USD 500,000 the roles usually separate.

   Why it matters here specifically

Indonesia has   no residential builder licensing regime and no statutory domestic building warranty  . Whatever protection you have is the contract and the money you have not yet paid.

That means the   valuation of work and the verification of payment milestones   is the mechanism through which you actually control the project. If the contractor certifies their own progress, you have no mechanism at all.

And a build supervised closely finishes better, faster and cheaper than one run remotely — substantially so. Owners who are not present and pay for nobody to be present get a building that varies from the drawings in ways they discover at handover, when leverage is gone.

   Where a QS earns their fee

  Comparing tenders properly.   Three quotes against a complete bill of quantities are comparable. Three quotes against a set of drawings are three different interpretations, and the cheapest is usually the one that excluded the most.

  Pricing variations before they happen.   Verbal variations priced afterwards are the single most common cause of dispute and budget overrun on Bali builds. A QS prices the c

t: How do you prepare a Bali villa for sale?
s: The paperwork takes longer than the presentation and matters more. Start it three months before you list.
b:
Most Bali sales that fall over do so at the document stage, weeks after a price was agreed, when a buyer's notary finds something the seller could have fixed months earlier. Preparing to sell here is mostly a paperwork exercise.

   Start with the documents, three months out

  Find the original certificate.   Not a copy. If it is with a notary, a bank or a family member, retrieve it now. If it is lost, replacement takes months and will stop a sale dead.

  Check the land office record matches.   Name, area, boundaries, encumbrances. Discrepancies between the certificate and the register are more common than buyers assume and take time to resolve.

  Bring PBB current.   Arrears transfer with the land, and a buyer's notary will find them. Clear them and keep the receipts.

  Locate the PBG and SLF.   If the building exists and these do not, you have a choice: regularise before listing, or discount for it. Regularising is usually cheaper than the discount a buyer will demand, and much cheaper than losing the sale at week six.

  Read your own lease, if you are selling a leasehold.   Specifically whether it permits assignment, whether the landowner's consent is required, and on what terms. If consent is needed, get it in principle before you list. A seller who discovers mid sale that the landowner wants a fee to consent has lost their negotiating position entirely.

  Resolve anything outstanding.   Boundary disagreements, unpaid contractors, disputes with neighbours over access. All of it surfaces in due diligence.

   Then the numbers

If the property has been rented, a buyer will want to see performance, and vague claims reduce the price rather than raise it.

Assemble two to three years of occupancy and revenue by month, the actual operating costs, the management agreement, and tax filings. A seller who produces this credibly commands a meaningfully better price than one who says the villa "does about USD 60,000 a year".

If the numbers are poor, you have a decisi

t: What happens in your first year owning a Bali villa?
s: The gap between the projection and the first twelve months is where most owners learn what they bought. Here is the sequence.
b:
The gap between the projection and the first twelve months is where most owners learn what they actually bought. The sequence is predictable enough to plan for.

   Months one to three: it costs money

  Nothing earns yet.   Even a purchased, furnished, ready villa needs listing, photography, pricing and a manager appointed before the first booking lands.

  You discover the defects.   Things the inspection missed or the previous owner lived with. A pool that loses water overnight. Drainage that only reveals itself in heavy rain. Aircon that cools inadequately in the room nobody tested. Budget for this — five to ten thousand dollars on an older property is normal, not unlucky.

  Fit out gaps.   Whatever you thought was included and was not. Linen sets, kitchen equipment, outdoor furniture that turned out to be at the end of its life.

  Licensing and administration.   NPWP, bank account if you are opening one, registering for the regional accommodation tax, sorting the operating position.

Net cash flow in this period is negative and it surprises people who modelled from month one.

   Months three to six: the listing is weak

  Platform ranking punishes you for being new.   A listing with two reviews sits below comparable villas with a hundred and forty. This is not about your villa; it is how the ranking works.

  Occupancy runs below your steady state  , frequently well below. Forty to fifty five percent in this window is normal for a good property that will eventually run at seventy five.

  Price below market deliberately.   The goal in these months is reviews, not revenue. Fifteen strong reviews earned at a discount are worth more than three bookings at full rate.

  You find out whether your manager is any good.   Response times, guest handling, the condition the villa is in when you look at it unannounced.

   Months six to twelve: it starts working

  Reviews accumulate and ranking improves.   Occupancy climbs toward the sustainable level.

  You learn you

t: What is it like having a baby in Bali?
s: Good private maternity care exists in the south. The paperwork after the birth is where foreign parents get caught.
b:
Plenty of foreign couples have children in Bali and the medical side is generally straightforward. The administrative side afterwards is where people find themselves in an unexpected situation.

   The medical picture

  Private hospitals in the south   — Denpasar, Kuta, Nusa Dua — provide competent maternity care with English speaking staff and international standard facilities. BIMC and Siloam are the names most foreign residents use.

  Midwife and birth centre options   exist, including in Ubud, with a more natural birth approach, and some foreign parents choose them.

  The ceiling applies here as elsewhere.   A complicated delivery, a premature baby needing advanced neonatal intensive care, or a serious maternal complication may require transfer. Establish in advance where you would go and confirm your insurance covers evacuation with a realistic limit.

  Maternity insurance   almost universally carries a   waiting period   — frequently ten to twelve months from policy start. If you are planning a family, arrange cover well before conceiving, because a policy taken out after a pregnancy begins will not cover it.

   The paperwork, which is the real subject

A birth in Indonesia generates Indonesian documentation, and a foreign child needs to be registered with their own country as well. Both have deadlines.

  The hospital birth notification  , issued at delivery.

  Indonesian birth certificate  , registered with the local civil registry (Dukcapil). There is a   time limit for registration   and late registration is considerably more difficult, so do not let this drift in the first sleep deprived weeks.

  Your embassy or consulate.   Registering the birth with your own country, and applying for the child's passport. Requirements and timelines vary by nationality and this is the step people underestimate.

  The child's immigration status.   A foreign child born in Indonesia needs a permit like any other foreign national. Typically a dependant permit attache

t: How do you make money on a Bali leasehold?
s: A wasting asset can still produce a return, but only if the income clears the decay. That arithmetic is the whole discipline.
b:
A leasehold loses value every year by design. Making money on one means the income has to outrun the decay, and that is a single calculation most buyers never run.

   The decay is the whole problem

You are not buying a property. You are buying a   defined number of years of use  , and each year that passes removes one.

On a thirty year lease over a USD 300,000 property, the term alone costs you roughly USD 10,000 a year in value. It appears on no statement, no invoice and no management report. It is the largest cost of ownership and it is invisible.

And the decline is not linear. It accelerates toward the end, because the pool of buyers willing to take a short remainder collapses. A villa with thirty years has a deep market. The same villa with eight has almost none.

   The calculation

  Over the years you actually hold, does the net income plus any use value exceed what you paid, with a margin?  

That is it. Everything else is detail.

Worked through on a real example:

Purchase at USD 250,000, twenty five years remaining. Transaction costs USD 12,000. Furnishing USD 35,000. Total in:   USD 297,000  .

Realistic net income after management at twenty percent, maintenance, staff, utilities, licensing, platform commission and tax:   USD 26,000 a year  .

Over twenty five years: USD 650,000, against USD 297,000 in. You recover your capital in   eleven and a half years   and the remaining thirteen and a half years are return.

That works, and it is not exciting, which is the point.

Now the same money on a fifteen year remainder in a better area, netting USD 31,000 because the location is stronger:

Over fifteen years: USD 465,000 against USD 297,000 in. Capital recovered in   nine and a half years  , with five and a half years of return.

Higher annual income, dramatically less total return, and at the end you have nothing to sell because a five year remainder has no buyer.

  The better location earns more per year and far less in total.   That is the trade at

t: How should you design outdoor space in a Bali villa?
s: Guests spend most of their time outside. The outdoor space is where the rate is set and where most villas underinvest.
b:
A guest in a Bali villa spends most of their waking time outside. The indoor space is where they sleep. Designing as though the reverse were true is the most common error in Bali villa design and it shows up directly in the rate.

   Why outdoor space sets the rate

  It is the cover image.   The pool with the villa behind it is what sells the booking, and everything around the pool is in that frame.

  It is what guests photograph   and post, which is free marketing.

  It is what they remember  , and what appears in reviews.

  It is what differentiates you   from fifty near identical villas with the same bedroom count. Indoor space is broadly similar across the market; outdoor space is not.

   The elements that matter

  The pool, and its relationship to everything else.   Not just its size. Where it sits relative to the living space, where the sun falls on it through the day, what you see from it, and what is in the frame behind it.

A generous pool with a poor relationship to the building photographs worse than a modest one placed well.

  A covered outdoor living area.   This is the most underprovided element in Bali villas and the most used. Somewhere to sit in shade, in rain, in the evening, with enough room to eat. Guests use it more than the interior.

  An outdoor dining table   that a group can actually sit around.

  Sun loungers   in the right number for the bedroom count, in a position where the sun is.

  Shade  , in more than one place, because a villa with no shade is unusable from eleven until three.

  An outdoor shower  , which photographs extremely well, costs very little, and is genuinely used near a beach.

  Lighting.   Uplighting on trees, path lighting, pool lighting. The cheapest transformation available and the thing most villas have none of. Evening photographs sell bookings that daytime ones do not.

  Garden  , which is a large part of what a Bali villa is selling and which appears in every frame.
