t: Do you need a land survey in Bali?
s: The advertised area, the certificate area and what is physically fenced are frequently three different numbers. A survey is how you find out.
b:
The single most common finding in Bali land due diligence is that the parcel is not the size everyone thought it was. A survey costs a few hundred dollars and it is skipped constantly.

   Why the numbers differ

  Old measurement.   Many Bali parcels were measured decades ago with methods that do not match modern survey accuracy.

  Informal family division.   Land passed through generations and divided by agreement, with fences and walls placed where they made sense rather than where a plan said.

  Encroachment.   A neighbour's wall, building or planting extending over the line, sometimes for years, sometimes deliberately.

  Erosion  , on coastal and riverside parcels, where the boundary is defined by a physical feature that has moved.

  Setbacks and access strips   that exist on the ground but were never reflected in the record.

  Simple error  , in a system with a great deal of manual record keeping.

The result is that the advertised area, the certificate area and the fenced area routinely differ, and the difference can be material.

   What a survey establishes

  The actual measured area   of the parcel.

  Where the boundaries physically are  , marked on the ground.

  Whether the certificate plan matches reality  , and where it does not.

  Encroachments  , in either direction.

  The relationship to setbacks   — road, boundary, river, coastal — and therefore what is genuinely buildable.

  Levels and slope  , which matter enormously for build cost on anything other than flat land.

   Why it matters commercially, not just legally

  You are paying per are.   If the parcel is 4.2 are rather than the 5 are advertised, you are overpaying by sixteen percent. That is a legitimate and entirely factual basis for renegotiating.

  Buildable area is what you are actually buying.   Subtract setbacks and any access strip, then apply KDB, and the number that remains determines what you can build. A large parcel with a river setback running through it may support l

t: How many bedrooms should a Bali villa have?
s: Revenue per bedroom falls as you add bedrooms, but total revenue rises and costs do not rise as fast. Where that crosses over is the whole decision.
b:
This is the most consequential design decision in a Bali rental villa, and it gets made on instinct far more often than on arithmetic.

   The pattern in the numbers

Nightly rate does not scale linearly with bedrooms. A one bedroom might achieve USD 90 a night. Two bedrooms does not get USD 180; it gets around USD 150. Three gets roughly USD 210, four around USD 280, five around USD 340.

Per bedroom, that is USD 90, USD 75, USD 70, USD 70, USD 68. Revenue per bedroom falls and then flattens.

But costs do not follow the same curve. One pool, one kitchen, one garden, one villa manager and broadly one cleaning team serve four bedrooms nearly as easily as they serve two. The fixed cost base is the villa, not the rooms.

So net income per bedroom improves as you add bedrooms, even though gross per bedroom falls. That is the argument for building larger, and it holds up to a point.

   Where it stops holding

Occupancy is the counterweight, and it moves the opposite way.

One and two bedroom villas in Bali serve couples and small groups, which is the deepest and most consistent demand pool in the market. They book year round, they book late, and they fill shoulder season.

Four, five and six bedroom villas serve families and groups. That demand is real and it pays well, but it is lumpier, more seasonal, books further ahead, and collapses harder in a quiet month. A five bedroom at sixty percent occupancy earns less than a three bedroom at eighty.

The other constraint is land. Bedrooms need footprint, and KDB limits how much of your plot you may build on. Adding a fifth bedroom often means a smaller pool or losing the garden, which are the two things that photograph the property and set the rate.

   The practical answer

  Three bedrooms is the most reliable configuration in Bali.   It serves couples travelling together, small families and groups of friends, which is the widest demand pool available. It sits inside most plot sizes without compromising the pool. It cost

t: How do off-market property deals work in Bali?
s: The best parcels frequently never reach a listing. Getting access means relationships, and it also means fewer checks have been done for you.
b:
A significant share of Bali's better transactions never appear on a website. Understanding why explains both the opportunity and the risk.

   Why good parcels stay off market

  Sellers who do not want attention.   A family selling inherited land, a foreign owner leaving quietly, a business selling premises. Listing invites questions they would rather not field.

  Agents with a buyer already.   A good parcel shown to three known buyers sells faster and more cleanly than one advertised to everyone, and the agent keeps control of the commission.

  Speed.   A seller who needs to complete quickly goes to people who can act, not to a portal.

  Price discovery.   Some sellers do not want a public number attached to their land, particularly where neighbours will hear it.

  It was never for sale.   The best land in Bali frequently belongs to people who had not considered selling until someone asked.

   What this means about listed stock

Not that everything listed is bad. Plenty of good property is openly marketed.

It does mean that a parcel which has been listed for eight months, at four different prices, through four agents, has been seen by a great many people who chose not to buy it. That is information.

The question worth asking of any listed property is:   why is this still available?  

Sometimes the answer is benign — the price is high, the seller is not motivated, the market is slow above a certain level. Sometimes it is a term, a permit, a zoning classification or a title problem that other buyers found.

   How to get access

  Tell people specifically what you want.   Not "something in Bali". A budget, an area, a plot size, a term, a purpose. Specific briefs get remembered; vague ones do not.

  Build relationships with two or three agents   rather than dealing with fifteen. An agent who believes you will actually transact brings you things first. An agent who has shown twenty people the same parcel brings you nothing.

  Talk to notaries.   They see tra

t: Is Berawa a good place to buy property?
s: Berawa has the highest occupancy in Canggu and the highest land prices. Whether it works depends entirely on what term you can get.
b:
Berawa is the most commercially developed part of Canggu and, by most measures, the strongest rental market on the island. It is also where the gap between rental performance and purchase price is narrowest.

   What Berawa is now

A dense strip running from the Canggu Shortcut down to Berawa Beach, with Atlas, Finns, La Brisa and a continuous run of restaurants, gyms, clinics and co working along it. It has the infrastructure of a small town and the traffic to match.

The guest profile is broad: couples, families, groups, digital nomads on longer stays, and a substantial repeat market. That breadth is what produces the occupancy, and it is the single strongest argument for the area.

   The numbers

Land in Berawa is among the most expensive in Bali outside of Seminyak's core and specific Bukit clifftop positions. Prices per are here have roughly doubled over five years and the corridor is effectively built out, which means new supply arrives by replacing existing buildings rather than by expanding.

Rental performance is correspondingly strong. Well run villas here achieve high occupancy across a longer season than most of Bali, with less of a February collapse than areas depending on a narrower guest type.

The problem is what that does to the purchase decision. High land price plus high rental income does not automatically mean a good investment. It means the return is already priced in, and the variable left to you is the lease term.

   The term problem

Because land is expensive, the leases available in Berawa at a given budget are shorter than they would be elsewhere.

At USD 250,000, Berawa offers a three bedroom with perhaps fifteen to eighteen years remaining. The same money in Pererenan or Cemagi offers the same house with twenty five to thirty. Berawa's higher income does not close a ten year gap in term. It rarely comes close.

This is the calculation that decides most Berawa purchases and it is usually made backwards, from the area's reputation rather

t: Can you homeschool in Bali?
s: A large community does it, the legal position for foreign children runs through immigration rather than education, and the practical question is accreditation.
b:
Bali has an unusually large homeschooling and alternative education community, driven partly by cost and partly by the kind of family that moves here.

   Why people do it

  International school fees are the largest single expense   for most foreign families in Bali, frequently exceeding housing.

  The community exists.   Canggu, Ubud and Sanur all have established homeschool networks, co ops, tutors and group activities, which removes the isolation that makes homeschooling hard elsewhere.

  Flexibility  , for families who travel or whose work moves.

  Alternative philosophies.   Bali attracts families interested in Montessori, Steiner, forest school and unschooling approaches, and there are established settings offering them.

   The legal position for foreign children

This is where people get confused, and the answer is simpler than expected.

  Your child's right to be in Indonesia runs through immigration, not education.   A foreign child needs a valid permit — typically a dependant permit attached to a parent's KITAS — regardless of whether they attend school, are homeschooled or do neither.

  Indonesian compulsory education law applies to Indonesian citizens.   A foreign child on a dependant permit is not within that framework in the same way, which is why homeschooling foreign children here is common and unremarkable.

  If one parent is Indonesian and the child holds Indonesian citizenship  , the position is different and worth taking advice on, because the child is within the Indonesian system.

   Accreditation, which is the real question

The legal position is straightforward. The practical one is not.

  What happens at fourteen, sixteen, eighteen?   A child needs recognised qualifications to enter university or employment, and "we homeschooled in Bali" is not a transcript.

The routes families use:

  An accredited distance programme   from the home country or an international provider, which issues recognised qualifications. This is the most comm

t: How do you extend a spouse KITAS?
s: The permit is sponsored by the marriage, so the extension turns on the marriage still existing and the sponsor still being able to sponsor.
b:
A spouse KITAS is the most stable residency route available to a foreigner in Indonesia, because it is not tied to a job. The extension still has to be done properly and on time.

   What the extension requires

Applied for   before expiry  , through your Indonesian spouse as sponsor.

Evidence that the basis still holds: the marriage subsisting, the sponsor's documents current, and the address record accurate.

The sponsor's   identity documents and family card   are part of the application, which means their paperwork being in order is part of your immigration position.

   Start early

A month to six weeks before expiry.

Spouse extensions depend on documents from third parties and on your sponsor's availability to sign and attend. A spouse travelling, working away, or simply busy in the week your permit expires is a problem you created by starting late.

Diarise the expiry at issue and diarise a start date a month before it.

   Where extensions fail

  Address record mismatches.   If you moved and did not update the   SKTT   and the permit record, the inconsistency surfaces here. Systems match strictly and reject rather than query.

  Sponsor document problems.   An expired ID, an out of date family card, or a marriage that was never properly reported and registered in Indonesia where it took place abroad. That last one catches couples who married overseas and assumed it was recognised automatically.

  Name inconsistencies   between the passport, the marriage certificate and earlier records.

  An agent who did not file.   Get the filing reference and receipt, not a reassurance.

   If the marriage ends

The permit is sponsored by the marriage. If the marriage ends by divorce or death, the basis for the permit ends with it.

There are rules about the period in which you must regularise your status or leave, and they are not generous. This is a genuinely difficult moment to be dealing with immigration administration, which is a reason to understand the position

t: What permit do family members need in Indonesia?
s: A spouse and children of a permit holder get residence through the sponsor, not work rights, and the permit ends when the sponsor's does.
b:
When one person in a family obtains a work, investor or retirement permit, the rest of the family is covered through a dependant arrangement rather than through permits of their own.

   What it covers

A   spouse   and   children   of a KITAS or KITAP holder, sponsored by that person rather than by an employer or an institution.

It permits   residence  . It does not permit work, and it does not create an independent position.

   The dependency, which is the defining feature

The permit is derived. If the principal's permit ends — employment finishes, a company closes, a renewal is missed, a sponsor withdraws —   the dependants' permits end with it.  

That has two practical consequences.

  Plan changes together.   A principal changing employer needs a new permit, and so does everyone attached to them. Arrange both before the old employment ends, not after.

  A gap affects everyone.   A late extension by the principal puts the whole family into overstay simultaneously, with a daily fine accruing   per person  , including children.

   What the application involves

  The principal's permit and sponsor documents.  

  Proof of relationship   — a marriage certificate for a spouse, birth certificates for children. Foreign documents need   legalisation   by apostille, since Indonesia is a party to the Hague Convention, and   sworn translation  .

  Address documentation  , and post arrival reporting including an   SKTT   for each family member.

  Personal documents   for each dependant.

Allow time. Legalising and translating foreign civil documents is slower than people expect and it is the step that delays most family applications.

   Work and study

  A dependant spouse cannot work   on the dependant permit. Employment requires the employer to obtain RPTKA approval and a work permit in the spouse's own name — which is a separate application and not automatic.

This catches couples where one partner has a job offer and the other assumes they can pick something u

t: How do you build a life in Bali?
s: The foreign community turns over constantly, and the relationship that matters most commercially is the one with your neighbours.
b:
People plan the visa, the house and the business, and then find that the hardest part of living in Bali is the part they never thought about.

   The transience

The foreign community in Bali turns over constantly.

People arrive with a plan, stay two years and leave. Someone you become close to takes a job in Singapore, or has a child and moves home, or simply runs out of reasons to stay.

  It happens repeatedly and it is wearing.   Long term residents describe it as the single hardest part of living here, and new arrivals almost never anticipate it.

Two practical responses: invest in the people who are actually staying, and build relationships that are not only with other foreigners.

   Where foreigners meet each other

  Around a thing rather than around being foreign.   Surfing, a gym, a sport, music, a class, a co working space, a school gate, volunteering.

Communities organised around an activity are more durable than ones organised around nationality, and they produce better friendships.

  Canggu and Pererenan   have the densest and youngest foreign population, heavily entrepreneurial and creative, with coworking spaces as the social infrastructure.

  Ubud   skews toward wellness, creative work and longer established residents.

  Sanur and Umalas   have more families and more people who have been here a long time.

  The Bukit   has a strong surf community with high repeat visitation and a settled core.

Where you live shapes who you meet more than anything else you do.

   The Indonesian community, which matters more

This is the part that separates people who live here from people who are staying here.

  Learn Bahasa Indonesia.   It is unusually learnable — no verb conjugation, no gender, no tones, phonetic spelling — and a few months of genuine effort produces functional conversation. It changes how you are treated, what people tell you, and what you understand about where you are.

  Know your neighbours.   Not as politeness. In Bali, the people a

t: Can you buy a Bali villa with a tenant in it?
s: Existing agreements bind you. A tenancy, a management contract or forward bookings all transfer with the property whether you wanted them or not.
b:
A villa that is already generating income looks like an advantage, and sometimes it is. What comes with it needs reading before you complete, because you inherit more than the building.

   What transfers with the property

  An existing tenancy.   A tenant with an unexpired agreement generally continues, and you become the landlord. If they paid twelve months in advance to the previous owner, you have a tenant for a year and no rent.

  A management agreement.   These frequently contain notice periods, termination fees and provisions about forward bookings. Some are drafted so a departing manager keeps or cancels the bookings, which is leverage you do not want them to have.

  Forward bookings.   Guests who booked and paid, sometimes months ahead. Those obligations are real and the money may already have been taken.

  Staff.   Long serving villa staff have accrued entitlements under Indonesian labour law — severance, service appreciation pay and compensation calculated on length of service. Whether that liability follows the property or stays with the seller depends on how it is structured, and it is frequently not addressed at all.

  Supplier and service contracts.   Pool service, garden, internet, licensing arrangements.

   What to ask for before agreeing anything

  Every agreement affecting the property, in full.   Not a summary, not a description. The documents.

  The tenancy  , with the term, the rent, what has been paid and when, the deposit and who holds it.

  The management agreement  , with fees, notice, termination and the forward booking provisions.

  The forward booking schedule  , with dates, amounts, what has been received and by whom, and what the cancellation terms are.

  Staff details   — how many, how long employed, on what terms, and what has been accrued.

  Two to three years of month by month revenue and costs  , with tax filings and bank statements behind them. A seller who cannot produce this has not proved the income and the price s

t: How do you set the nightly rate for a Bali villa?
s: Most owners price off the listing prices of neighbours, which are not what those villas achieve. Here is the method that actually works.
b:
Pricing is the highest leverage thing an owner controls and the thing most owners spend the least time on. A twelve percent improvement in average rate is a twelve percent improvement in revenue with no additional cost, and it is routinely available.

   Stop pricing off listed rates

The most common method in Bali is to look at three similar villas nearby, see what they list at, and price just under.

That fails because listed rates are asking prices. A villa listing at USD 250 might be averaging USD 165 after discounts, long stay rates, direct bookings and empty nights. Pricing "just under" its listing means pricing well above what it actually achieves, which is why so many well presented Bali villas sit at forty percent occupancy wondering why.

What you want is achieved rate, not listed rate. You get it by watching a set of comparable villas' availability calendars over six to eight weeks and noting which dates fill and at what price. Tedious, and it is the only reliable source.

   Build the rate from the calendar, not the year

Bali does not have one rate. It has at least four.

  Peak   — July, August, and roughly 20 December to 5 January. Demand exceeds supply. Rates run forty to seventy percent above base, minimum stays go to three to five nights, and you should be close to full.

  High   — May, June, September, early October. Strong demand, rates ten to twenty five percent above base, occupancy in the eighties for a well run property.

  Base   — March, April, mid October, November.

  Low   — late January, February. The rainy season trough. Rates fifteen to twenty five percent below base, and this is where occupancy is won or lost.

Setting one rate for the year means you undercharge for a third of it and overcharge for another third. That single error costs more than most owners' entire management fee.

   Work out your floor before anything else

Your floor is the rate below which a booking costs you money.

t: What is property like in Petitenget and Batu Belig?
s: The strip between Seminyak and Canggu has the amenity of both and the traffic of neither. It is the most underrated position in the south.
b:
Petitenget and Batu Belig occupy the stretch between Seminyak's northern edge and the Canggu river mouth. They are frequently skipped by buyers who look at Seminyak and then at Canggu and never stop in between.

   What the area is

Petitenget runs north from Seminyak along Jalan Petitenget, a continuous run of established restaurants, beach clubs and hotels. Batu Belig continues north to the beach of the same name, becoming lower density and more residential as it goes.

The character is more grown up than Canggu and less relentless than Seminyak's centre. The guest profile skews older and higher spending: couples, families, people who want walkable dining without the scooter density of Berawa.

Beach access at Batu Belig is genuinely good, and the sunset stretch here is one of the better ones in the south.

   Why it is underrated

Three things.

  Location.   It sits between the two strongest demand centres in Bali with road access to both. A guest can reach Seminyak's restaurants and Canggu's beach clubs in ten to fifteen minutes.

  Established infrastructure.   Unlike the northern Canggu corridor, this area was built out years ago. Roads, drainage and utilities are in a different condition to what you find in Pererenan or Seseh. That matters more than buyers expect, particularly in the rainy season.

  Pricing.   Land here is cheaper than Seminyak's core and, on some streets, cheaper than Berawa, for a position with comparable amenity and better infrastructure.

   What the market looks like

Stock is largely existing villas rather than new development, because the area is built out. That has an advantage and a cost: what you buy exists and can be inspected, but new build opportunities are rare and land rarely trades.

Villas here are often ten to twenty years old. The build quality of that generation is variable and renovation is frequently part of the purchase. Budget for it rather than discovering it.

t: Is Tanah Lot a good place to buy?
s: A famous temple, a championship golf course, black sand coast and land at a fraction of Canggu. The demand has not arrived at the same speed.
b:
Tanah Lot is one of the most photographed places in Indonesia and one of the least developed coastal property markets within reach of Canggu.

   What it is

A sea temple on a rock formation off the Tabanan coast, reached at low tide and surrounded at high, with a visitor economy built around sunset.

Behind it sits a   championship golf course  , rice terraces running inland, black sand beaches and a scattering of resorts and villas.

It is in   Tabanan regency  , roughly twenty to thirty five minutes north of Canggu depending on traffic, and an hour or more from the airport.

   The visitor pattern, which is the commercial problem

Tanah Lot receives an enormous number of visitors and almost all of them   arrive in the late afternoon, watch the sunset and leave  .

Day trip volume does not produce accommodation demand. The temple is a stop on an itinerary rather than a destination people stay at, and that has been true for decades.

So the visitor numbers are impressive and largely irrelevant to a villa owner. Underwriting on them is the most common mistake in this area.

   Where the actual demand is

  Golf.   The course is a genuine draw and golf visitors stay several nights. It is a specific, reliable and underserved market, and a well presented property near the course serving it is a defensible business.

  Quiet seeking families and couples   who have done Canggu and want space, a beach and less density, and who accept the drive.

  Weddings and events  , given the setting, though that requires the property and the licensing to support it.

What is absent: any nomad market, any walkable amenity, any long stay foreign resident base, and any year round demand floor. The quiet months are genuinely quiet.

   The market

Land is   substantially cheaper than Canggu   and cheaper than Seseh, with generous plots and among the longest available lease terms in the coastal corridor.

Finished stock is limited. This is a land and build market.

t: What should a villa inspection cover in Bali?
s: A walkthrough at midday tells you almost nothing. The things that cost money are structural, hidden and visible only if you look for them.
b:
Most Bali villa purchases involve one viewing, in the middle of the day, in dry weather, guided by the person selling it. That is not an inspection.

   Engage someone independent

An architect or building surveyor you engaged, not one the agent introduced, for a few hundred dollars against a purchase of hundreds of thousands.

Allow   a full day  , and go back at different times — after rain, in the evening — because drainage and noise reveal themselves on a schedule.

Bring the   certificate, the drawings and the permits  , and check the building against them rather than against your impression.

   The documents first

  PBG  , issued, matching the building that physically exists.

  SLF  , the certificate of fitness. Without it the building is not lawfully occupiable and it is materially harder to sell.

  As built drawings  , if they exist, showing what was actually constructed.

  PBB receipts  , current, because arrears attach to the land.

A building larger than its approval, or with no approval, is a liability you would be buying. Regularising is sometimes possible and sometimes — where zoning does not permit what was built — it is not.

   Water, which is where Bali buildings fail

  Run every tap, shower and toilet.   Check pressure at the   highest point   of the building, which is where it fails.

  Test hot water everywhere  , from cold.

  Flood the shower trays and wet areas   and leave them. Come back and look at the ceiling below.

  Look at every ceiling   for staining, which is the evidence of a leak whether or not it is leaking today.

  Check the roof   and the guttering, and ask what the roof is and when it was last done. Alang alang thatch has a finite life and replacement is a significant job.

  Inspect drainage   around the building and across the site. If it has not rained, run hoses. Bali rainfall is not gentle and inadequate drainage is the most expensive defect to fix after the fact.

   The pool

  Does the water level hold overnight?

t: How do you register a birth abroad with Indonesia?
s: Events that happened abroad have to be reported in Indonesia to have effect here, and the deadlines are shorter than people expect.
b:
A marriage or a birth that happened in Australia, the UK or anywhere else is not automatically recognised in Indonesia. It has to be reported, and the reporting has deadlines.

   Why it matters

  For a spouse KITAS  , the marriage must be recognised here. A couple who married abroad and never reported it find out at the visa application, or at the extension, which is a bad moment.

  For a child's citizenship  , where one parent is Indonesian, the birth has to be reported for the child's Indonesian status to be registered. Missing this can compromise the dual citizenship position, which under the   2006 citizenship law   runs until age eighteen plus a declaration period.

  For property  , because an Indonesian citizen can hold   Hak Milik   freehold and a foreigner cannot. A child whose Indonesian citizenship was never properly registered may lose an entitlement that matters enormously later.

  For inheritance  , where establishing who is entitled depends on recognised relationships.

  For the marital property agreement  , which determines whether an Indonesian spouse can hold freehold cleanly at all — and which sits on top of a marriage that has to be recognised first.

   Reporting a marriage contracted abroad

Where an Indonesian citizen marries abroad, the marriage generally must be   reported to the Indonesian representative   in that country, and then   registered in Indonesia   with the civil registry on return.

  There are time limits  , and late reporting is considerably more difficult than timely reporting.

Documents required typically include the foreign marriage certificate,   legalised   — by apostille, since Indonesia is a party to the Hague Convention — and   translated by a sworn translator  , along with both parties' identity documents.

   Reporting a birth abroad

Where a child is born abroad to an Indonesian citizen parent, the birth is reported to the Indonesian representative in that country and registered here.

Again there are   time l

t: What mental health support exists in Bali?
s: Good support exists and is thinner than at home. Knowing where it is before you need it is the useful step.
b:
People move to Bali for a better life and a meaningful number find the first year harder than expected. The support exists; it is thinner than at home and most people have not located it before they need it.

   Why it is harder than it looks

  Isolation.   Working remotely from a villa is a very different thing from a holiday. No colleagues, no structure, no incidental contact. People who arrive without a job to go to, a school gate or a team frequently underestimate this.

  Transience.   The foreign community turns over constantly. You become close to someone and they leave, repeatedly. Long term residents consistently name this as the hardest part of living here.

  The gap between expectation and reality.   A permanent version of a two week holiday does not exist. Traffic, the wet season, administration and the cost of living here lawfully are all invisible from a sun lounger, and the adjustment is real.

  Alcohol.   It is everywhere in the foreign social scene, particularly in Canggu, and for some people that is a genuine problem worth naming rather than talking around.

  Distance from family  , and time zones that make ordinary contact awkward.

  Financial pressure  , where a business or a property is not performing as planned in a place where everyone appears to be doing well.

   What exists here

  English speaking counsellors and psychologists   practise in Bali, particularly in Canggu, Seminyak, Sanur and Ubud, both in person and online. Quality and qualification vary and it is worth checking credentials rather than assuming.

  Psychiatric care   is available privately in Denpasar and the south, and is more limited than in most home countries.

  Online therapy   with a practitioner in your own country, which for many people is the practical answer — familiar language, familiar context, no local availability constraint. Time zones are the friction.

  Support groups  , including addiction recovery groups, meet in the main areas and are more establis

t: Villa, apartment or townhouse in Bali?
s: The three property types carry different titles, different licences and completely different exit markets. The building is the least important difference.
b:
Buyers compare these three on layout and price. The differences that actually matter are legal and structural, and they show up years later at the exit.

   Villa

A standalone building on its own plot, with its own pool in most cases, and its own land right underneath it.

  Title.   Leasehold over the land, Hak Pakai if you hold residency and the value threshold is met, or HGB held by a PT PMA. You control the land right directly.

  Control.   Total. You decide on renovation, management, pricing and when to sell. No committee, no service charge, no shared decisions.

  Income.   The highest gross and net of the three, and the widest range of outcomes. A well run villa outperforms everything. A badly run one underperforms an apartment.

  Costs.   The highest. Pool maintenance, garden, staff, structural upkeep, insurance. Expect fifteen to twenty five percent of gross revenue before management fees.

  Exit.   The deepest resale market in Bali by a large margin. Villas are what buyers come here looking for.

   Apartment

A unit within a building, usually with shared facilities and a body corporate running them.

  Title.   Strata title —  Hak Milik atas Satuan Rumah Susun  — over the unit, with the land held collectively. Foreigners may hold strata title over an apartment subject to a minimum value threshold, and in practice most foreign apartment ownership in Bali runs through leasehold or a company anyway.

  Control.   Limited. A building committee makes decisions about the common property, the service charge is set collectively, and your ability to renovate is constrained.

  Income.   Lower gross than a villa of equivalent value, but lower costs and much lower management burden. Occupancy is often higher because the price point serves a bigger market.

  Costs.   Service charge, which is predictable and unavoidable, plus a sinking fund for building works. Considerably simpler than running a villa.

  Exit.   The narrowest market of the three in Bali. Apartme

t: Can you earn passive income from Bali property?
s: It is income, and it is not passive. Knowing exactly how much attention it needs is the difference between a good year and a bad one.
b:
"Passive income" is the phrase that sells most Bali property, and it is the one I would push back on hardest. The income is real. The passivity is not, and the properties that perform are the ones whose owners understood that from the start.

   What it actually takes

A short let villa in Bali is a hospitality business with one unit. Somebody has to handle:

Pricing across four distinct seasons. Guest communication, often across time zones and at short notice. Check in and check out. Cleaning and laundry between every stay. Pool chemistry, weekly at minimum. Garden maintenance in a climate that grows things fast. Staff management, scheduling and payroll. Repairs, which in a humid tropical environment arrive more often than owners expect. Platform listings, photography refreshes, review management. Licensing and tax filings. Restocking consumables.

You can pay someone to do all of it. You cannot make it stop needing to be done, and you cannot fully delegate the judgement about whether it is being done well.

   The management fee reality

A full service villa manager in Bali charges fifteen to twenty five percent of gross revenue, sometimes more for smaller properties. Some structures add a fixed monthly fee on top, and some mark up maintenance.

At twenty percent of a USD 70,000 gross, that is USD 14,000 a year. Add maintenance, utilities, staff, licensing, platform commission and tax and you are commonly at forty to fifty percent of gross before you see anything.

That is not a criticism of managers. Running a villa well is genuinely difficult and the good ones earn it. It is a correction to the arithmetic, because most projections handed to buyers do not include it properly.

   Where the passive version breaks

  The manager underperforms and you do not notice.   The most common failure. Occupancy drifts from seventy five to fifty five percent over two years, revenue falls, and nobody tells you because the manager's incentive is the easy life, not the marginal

t: What happens when a Bali lease expires?
s: The building passes with the land, your right to be there ends, and whatever you did not negotiate decades earlier is what you get.
b:
Most Bali leaseholds have not reached expiry yet, because the foreign buying wave is younger than the terms. The first large cohort is approaching it, and what happens is entirely determined by wording agreed decades ago.

   The default

  Your right to occupy ends.  

  The building passes with the land   to the landowner, unless the contract provides otherwise. You funded the villa; at expiry it is theirs.

  You have no claim for the value of what you built  , unless a compensation mechanism was written in.

That is not a scandal. It is the ordinary operation of a lease and it is why leasehold is priced below the alternatives. The problem is that buyers fund a build believing they own a villa, when what they own is a defined number of years of using one.

   What you actually have at expiry

Whatever the deed says. In practice, one of four positions:

  A guaranteed extension —  jaminan perpanjangan .   The landowner is contractually bound to extend, on terms already agreed, at a price or formula fixed at the outset. You extend and carry on. This is the good outcome and it is the least common.

  A right of first refusal —  prioritas perpanjangan .   You get to negotiate, at a price set at the moment your only alternative is walking away from a building you paid for. The landowner knows exactly what your alternative is worth, which is nothing. Extension prices at multiples of the original premium are not unusual, and the lease was honoured exactly as written.

  A compensation mechanism  , where the building passes but the landowner pays an agreed valuation or formula. Rare, and worth negotiating for.

  Nothing.   The lease ends, you hand over the keys.

   The decline before you get there

The expiry itself is the end of a process that costs you throughout.

A leasehold is a   wasting asset   and the decline is   not linear  . It accelerates toward the end, because the pool of buyers willing to take a short remainder collapses.

A villa with thirty years left

t: What is an SKCK and when do you need one?
s: A police certificate required for some permits, some employment and some licensing, obtained locally and frequently left until it delays something.
b:
The   SKCK   —  Surat Keterangan Catatan Kepolisian  — is the Indonesian police certificate confirming an absence of recorded criminal history. It appears in more processes than people expect and it is rarely arranged in advance.

   When it is needed

  Some immigration applications  , depending on the permit type and current requirements.

  Employment  , particularly with larger employers, in regulated sectors and in anything involving children.

  Some business licensing  , depending on the activity.

  Certain civil registration processes.  

  Volunteer placements  , especially those involving vulnerable people, where a clearance is both a requirement and a sign that the organisation is operating properly.

Requirements change and differ by process. Confirm what the specific application actually needs rather than obtaining one speculatively — though obtaining one early is generally better than discovering you need it.

   Getting one in Indonesia

Applied for through the police, at a level appropriate to the purpose — local, regency, provincial or national depending on what the receiving authority requires. A certificate issued at too low a level will be rejected.

You will generally need your   passport  , your   stay permit  , address documentation such as the   SKTT  , photographs to a specified standard, and fingerprinting.

It has a   validity period  , after which it expires and must be reissued. Obtaining one a year ahead of when you need it is not useful.

   The clearance from your home country

Separately, many Indonesian processes want a police certificate from your   country of nationality or previous residence  , not just an Indonesian one.

That is obtained from your home authority — a national police check in Australia, an ACRO certificate in the UK, an FBI identity history summary in the United States — and it then needs:

  Legalisation   by apostille, since Indonesia is a party to the Hague Convention, or consular legalisation where applicabl

t: Is Munggu or Tumbak Bayuh worth buying?
s: The rice fields immediately inland from the Pererenan corridor, cheaper than the coast and close enough to use it.
b:
Munggu and Tumbak Bayuh sit inland from Pererenan and Seseh, in the rice fields between the coast road and the interior. They are where buyers go when the coastal corridor has priced them out.

   What they are

Working agricultural villages with rice terraces, small roads and a growing scatter of villa development among them.

  Munggu   is closer to the coast and to the Pererenan corridor.   Tumbak Bayuh   sits inland toward Kerobokan and the Canggu shortcut.

Both are five to fifteen minutes from the beach at Pererenan or Seseh, and fifteen to thirty from Canggu's centre depending on traffic.

There is no walkable strip. A handful of cafes have appeared, and you drive for anything substantial.

   The market

Land is   meaningfully cheaper than the coastal strip   at Pererenan or Seseh, with larger plots and longer available lease terms at the same budget.

There is genuine supply, which is increasingly rare this close to the Canggu corridor.

Stock is a mix of new villa development aimed at investors and local housing. This is more of a build market than a buy market.

   The zoning constraint, which is the defining issue

This is the whole subject in these areas and it is why the land is cheaper.

  A great deal of Munggu and Tumbak Bayuh land remains classified agricultural.   Rice fields are agricultural land, and commercial accommodation is not permitted in a green zone.

The fact that villas exist nearby is not evidence that your parcel permits one. Some were built before enforcement tightened, some are in pockets of residential zoning, and some are operating in a position their owners would rather not have examined.

  Check the spatial plan for the exact parcel   with Badung regency before anything else. This is the single most important step in this area and it is the one that determines whether the land is worth anything to you.

   Rental performance

Moderate, and dependent on what you build.

The guest is someone who wants rice field views, space, qu

t: Where do you shop for food in Bali?
s: Local produce is cheap, imported goods are not, and the gap between the two is most of the difference in anyone's cost of living here.
b:
The single largest variable in what living in Bali costs is how much of your shopping is imported. People who eat locally spend very little; people who replicate a Western supermarket basket spend a great deal.

   The tiers

  Traditional markets (pasar).   Fruit, vegetables, eggs, spices, fish and meat, at the lowest prices available. Early morning is when the produce is best. Prices are negotiable and foreigners are quoted higher until they are known — which is one more practical argument for learning some Bahasa Indonesia.

  Local supermarkets and minimarkets.   Everyday Indonesian products at ordinary prices, on every corner.

  Expat oriented supermarkets   in Canggu, Seminyak, Umalas and Sanur, carrying imported cheese, meat, dairy, cereals, wine and Western brands. Convenient, well stocked, and where the money goes.

  Organic and health food stores  , particularly in Canggu and Ubud, with a strong plant based and specialist offering at premium prices.

  Online grocery delivery  , which has expanded substantially and covers most of the south.

   The price gap

  Local produce is genuinely cheap.   Tropical fruit, vegetables, rice, eggs, chicken, local fish and tofu cost a fraction of European or Australian prices.

  Imported goods carry duty, freight and a premium.   Cheese, butter, beef, wine, spirits, breakfast cereals, chocolate and most branded Western products cost meaningfully more than at home — in some cases several times more.

  Alcohol is expensive.   Indonesia applies substantial duties on imported alcohol, and wine and spirits in particular are considerably more expensive than in Australia or Europe. Local beer and arak are cheap.

That gap is where a Bali food budget is decided. Two people eating largely local spend very little; two people shopping an imported basket spend close to what they would at home.

   Eating out

  Warungs   serve local food at prices that make cooking at home barely worth the effort for one person.

t: How do you extend an investor KITAS?
s: The permit rests on the company, so the extension turns on the company's compliance as much as on your own paperwork.
b:
An investor KITAS is granted on the basis of a shareholding in an Indonesian company. That makes the extension a company question as much as a personal one, which is what catches people whose own documents are immaculate.

   What the extension requires

Applied for   before expiry  , through the sponsoring company.

Evidence that the basis still holds: the shareholding intact and still meeting the   investment threshold  , the company active, and your position in it unchanged.

Thresholds have moved. Verify the current requirement rather than assuming the figure that applied when you first obtained the permit still applies.

   The company's compliance is your immigration position

This is the point.

A sponsoring PT PMA with   missed quarterly LKPM reports, outstanding tax filings, an inactive NIB or a KBLI classification that no longer matches what it does   has a standing problem, and it attaches to the permits it sponsors.

An investor with perfect personal paperwork, sponsored by a company three quarters behind on LKPM, has an extension problem that is not about them.

  Ask your corporate service provider to confirm the company's filings are current  , in writing, a couple of months before your renewal. That is your immigration diligence, not just their administration.

   Start early

A month to six weeks before expiry.

The application depends on company documents, a director's signature and evidence assembled by third parties. Leaving it to the last fortnight is how people end up in overstay, with a daily fine from day one and escalation to detention and a re entry ban past a threshold measured in weeks.

   What the permit actually permits

  Residency on the basis of an investment. Not a general work authorisation.  

The scope is narrower than many holders assume. Performing an operational role in the company — managing staff, directing work, delivering services — generally engages the foreign worker framework and   RPTKA   approval.

t: Who actually books Bali villas?
s: Different parts of Bali serve different guests with different booking behaviour. Buying in the wrong area for your property type costs you occupancy.
b:
Bali is not one rental market. It is several, and they behave differently enough that a villa which fills easily in one area would struggle two corridors away.

   The main guest groups

  Australians.   The largest and most consistent source market, and the most seasonal. School holidays drive their calendar hard: late June through July, late September, and the December January peak. They book families and groups, favour Seminyak, Canggu, Uluwatu and increasingly the Bukit, and they return. Repeat rates are high.

  Europeans.   Longer stays, less concentrated in school holidays, and stronger in the May to September window when Europe is warm but Bali is dry. They skew toward Ubud, the Bukit and Canggu, and they research more before booking, which means your listing quality matters more with this group.

  Asian regional travellers   from Singapore, Malaysia, Korea, Japan and increasingly China and India. Shorter stays, often long weekends, and a strong preference for Seminyak, Nusa Dua and the developed south. Higher expectations around service and facilities, and much less interested in a remote villa down a dirt road.

  Digital nomads and long stayers.   Concentrated in Canggu, Pererenan and Ubud. Monthly bookings, price sensitive, care about internet and workspace far more than pool size. They fill low season, which is precisely when you need filling.

  Surf travellers.   The Bukit — Uluwatu, Bingin, Padang Padang, Balangan — and the Canggu to Seseh coast. Season driven by swell rather than holidays, which means they fill different weeks than everyone else. Loyal, repeat heavy, and often book direct.

  Wellness and retreat visitors.   Ubud primarily. Book through programmes and retreats rather than platforms, which changes how you reach them entirely.

   What this means area by area

  Canggu and Pererenan.   The broadest mix, which is why occupancy is the steadiest. Nomads fill the quiet months, Australians and Europeans fill the peaks. Two and three bedro

t: Is Cemagi worth buying in?
s: Between Pererenan and Seseh, with a black sand beach, a temple on the point and less density than anywhere south of it.
b:
Cemagi sits immediately north of Pererenan, before Seseh, on the stretch of coast where the Canggu corridor thins out.

   What it is

Black sand beach with a temple on the headland, rice fields running back inland, and villa development that is present but nothing like Canggu's density.

  Gria Beach   and the Cemagi shoreline are quieter than anything to the south, and the area retains a working agricultural character that Pererenan has largely lost.

Ten to fifteen minutes to Pererenan's amenity, twenty to thirty five to Canggu's centre depending on traffic.

There is no walkable strip — a handful of beach clubs and cafes have appeared, and you drive for anything substantial.

   The market

Land is   cheaper than Pererenan   and more available, with larger plots and lease terms that run meaningfully longer at the same budget.

Prices have moved substantially as Pererenan matured and pushed demand north, so a good deal of the growth story is already in the number.

Stock is a mix of newer villa development aimed at investors and land. This is more of a build market than a buy market.

   Rental performance

Real and improving, sitting between Pererenan's established demand and Seseh's emerging one.

The guest wants quiet, space and a beach, and accepts a short drive to amenity. That market has grown as Canggu has densified and as families and repeat visitors have looked for something calmer.

  What is absent   is walkable demand and the digital nomad long stay population that fills Canggu's February and March. Occupancy is more seasonal than the prime corridor, and a projection built on Canggu comparables will overstate it.

Properties that perform are larger, well designed villas with good pools and rice field or ocean outlook — the things that justify the drive. Small units without a view compete poorly against a much larger market to the south.

   The zoning issue

t: Should you buy land or a finished villa in Bali?
s: Building saves fifteen to twenty-five percent and starts with a full term. It costs you eighteen months, real attention and permit risk.
b:
This is the decision that most determines your outcome, and it is usually made on temperament rather than arithmetic.

   What buying finished gives you

  It exists.   You can inspect it, check the permits against the building, see the finish, walk the street at different times and verify the actual rental performance from real accounts.

  Speed.   Weeks rather than two years. Income from the first season.

  Known cost.   No overrun, no variations argument, no contractor risk.

  Discoverable risk.   Remaining term, building condition, zoning, permits, access — every one is checkable in a fortnight by a competent notary and a surveyor.

  A track record  , if it has been let. Two years of verified month by month revenue is worth far more than any projection.

   What building gives you

  A full term from the start.   This is the largest advantage and it is underweighted. Buying a finished villa means buying somebody's remainder — fifteen, eighteen, twenty two years. Building on a new lease starts at thirty.

On a leasehold, term is the investment. Ten extra years is worth more than almost anything about the building.

  No developer margin.   You typically save   fifteen to twenty five percent   against the equivalent finished property.

  Specification you chose  , designed for how villas actually earn — pool relationship, outdoor living, plot use against KDB, aircon sizing, drainage — rather than what someone else built.

  No accumulated maintenance.   Much of Bali's existing stock is ten to twenty years old, with pools, roofs, electrics and aircon reaching end of life together.

   What building costs you

  Eighteen to twenty four months   from land purchase to first guest.

  Real attention.   A build supervised closely finishes better and cheaper than one run remotely, substantially so. Either be here for much of it or pay an architect or project manager five to ten percent for genuine site supervision.

  Permit risk.   Zoning, KDB, setbacks, PBG, SLF. A

t: How do you secure a Bali villa?
s: Most losses in Bali villas are opportunistic and preventable. The fix is layered and cheap, and guests notice when it is absent.
b:
Bali is a relatively safe place and villa break ins do happen. Almost all of them are opportunistic rather than planned, which means the response is prevention rather than defence.

   What actually gets taken

Phones, laptops, cameras, cash and passports left visible. Bags near an open door. Scooters. Items from an unsecured outdoor area.

The pattern is someone walking past an open gate or an unlocked sliding door and taking what is within reach. Forced entry is far less common than opportunity.

That tells you where to spend.

   The layers that matter

  A perimeter.   A wall or fence with a gate that closes and locks. This does more than anything else, because it removes the opportunity before it reaches the building.

  Lighting.   Motion activated lights around the perimeter and entrances. Cheap, effective, and it also improves the property at night for guests.

  Locks that work.   Sliding doors in Bali villas are frequently the weak point — many can be lifted out of the track or opened with minimal effort. Proper locks and anti lift blocks cost very little.

  A safe.   Bolted, in a wardrobe, large enough for a laptop. Guests use them if they exist and leave valuables on the bed if they do not. This is the single highest return item for guest facing properties.

  Cameras   at the entrance and perimeter, not inside. Be explicit in the listing about where cameras are — undisclosed interior cameras are a serious breach of guest trust and of platform rules, and they end badly.

  Someone present.   A night security presence, or a caretaker living on site, which is common in Bali and which deters almost everything.

   Staff versus service

  Employing security directly   brings the full Indonesian employment framework — BPJS, THR, overtime, leave, and the termination provisions foreign employers consistently underestimate. Manageable, and a permanent commitment.

  A security service   costs more per hour and the employment obligations sit with them.

t: What are the warning signs on a Bali property?
s: Most losses here are preceded by the same handful of signals. None of them are subtle once you know what they are.
b:
The losses in this market are not caused by sophisticated fraud. They are preceded by signals that were visible and that the buyer talked themselves past.

   The signals that should stop a transaction

  Pressure to move faster than one to three weeks of due diligence.   The single most reliable warning sign in Bali. Genuine sellers of genuine property expect verification. The only people who need you to move today are the ones who need you to move before you look.

  "Freehold for foreigners."   There is no such thing. The description tells you what kind of counterparty you are dealing with before you look at anything else.

  Any structure whose purpose is to let you control land you cannot lawfully hold.   Nominee arrangements, a local company with side agreements, a foundation holding property for your benefit. Void under Indonesian law, prohibited to facilitate under Perda Bali 4/2026, and when they fail they fail completely.

  A deposit requested to an individual's personal account.   Deposits belong with your own notary, against written conditions, refundable if due diligence discloses a defect.

  Refusal to let you engage your own notary  , or insistence that the seller's or the agent's is used for everything. That notary is the only independent check available to you.

  A seller who is not the registered owner   with no valid, current power of attorney connecting them.

  Original certificate unavailable.   A photocopy proves nothing, and a lost certificate takes months to replace and stops a sale dead.

   The ones that mean renegotiate, not necessarily walk

  A short remaining term at a prime area price.   Not a defect, a mispricing. The area does not extend the term.

  An extension clause that is  prioritas  rather than  jaminan .   You are buying the initial term and nothing more. Price it as that.

  "Extendable at market rate."   Worth almost nothing, because market rate is determined at the moment your only alternative is abandoning a building

t: Is Tuban or Benoa worth buying?
s: Minutes from the terminal, unfashionable, and priced accordingly. The commercial logic is different from everywhere else in Bali.
b:
Tuban and Benoa sit either side of the airport, and almost no foreign buyer considers them. The reasons are partly sound and partly habit.

   What they are

  Tuban   runs from Kuta's southern end along the coast to the airport, dense with hotels, the Discovery mall and a working commercial strip. The beach here is long and the sunsets are the same ones people pay Seminyak prices for.

  Benoa   sits on the eastern side, around the harbour, with the Bali Mandara toll road connecting to Nusa Dua and Sanur. More industrial in character, with the port, watersports operations and a spread of hotels.

Both are   five to fifteen minutes from Ngurah Rai  , which is the defining commercial fact.

   Why nobody looks

Fashion. Foreign buyers went Seminyak, Canggu, Pererenan, and the airport corridor was never on the list.

Aircraft noise, which is real and which people assume is worse and more uniform than it actually is.

An association with mass tourism and transit rather than lifestyle.

   The commercial logic

  Airport proximity is a genuine, underrated asset.  

The Bukit is forty five to ninety minutes from the terminal. Canggu is similar and worsening. A guest arriving at 11pm after a long flight, or leaving on a 6am departure, values fifteen minutes enormously.

That produces a specific and uncontested market:   first and last night stays  , crew and business travellers, and anyone on a short stopover. Nobody in Canggu competes for it because they cannot.

  Volume over rate.   The product that works here is mid market accommodation, apartments and small hotels serving consistent volume at a modest nightly rate. Not premium villas.

  Commercial property.   High footfall retail and food and beverage on the Tuban strip serving a large hotel population.

  Long term rental   to the substantial workforce employed in the airport, hotel and tourism industries, which is year round and does not care about the season.

   The noise question, honestly

t: How does an Indonesian passport work for dual nationals?
s: A child of a mixed marriage can hold both until eighteen. After the declaration period, one goes, and which one decides whether they can ever own land here.
b:
Indonesia does not generally permit dual nationality. The main exception runs through childhood and ends with a deadline that families miss.

   The window

Under the   2006 citizenship law  , a child of a marriage between an Indonesian citizen and a foreign national may hold   limited dual citizenship until the age of eighteen  , plus a period afterwards — commonly described as up to three years — within which the child must   declare   which nationality they choose.

During that window the child can hold   both passports  , travel on either, and is treated as Indonesian in Indonesia.

  If no declaration is made within the period, the Indonesian citizenship is generally lost.  

   Why it matters more than an identity question

  An Indonesian citizen can hold Hak Milik, Indonesian freehold. No foreigner can, ever, under any structure.  

So the declaration at eighteen decides whether that person can own land in Indonesia for the rest of their life.

For a family with property here, that is an inheritance and asset holding decision. A child who declares foreign nationality becomes a   foreign heir  , and where a foreigner becomes entitled to Indonesian freehold through inheritance, disposal rules apply within a defined period.

A child who retains Indonesian citizenship does not have that problem.

   Getting it right from the start

  Register the child's status properly.   Where the birth occurred abroad, it must be   reported to the Indonesian representative   in that country and registered here, within time limits. Documents need   legalisation   — by apostille, since Indonesia is a party to the Hague Convention — and   sworn translation  .

A child whose Indonesian status was never registered may not have the dual position at all, which removes the choice before it is ever made.

  Obtain the Indonesian passport   and keep it current through childhood, because it is the practical evidence of the status.

t: Is Sawangan or Melasti worth buying?
s: White sand, calm water, big resorts and land cheaper than the western clifftops, on the side of the Bukit most buyers never look at.
b:
The Bukit has two coasts and foreign buyers overwhelmingly look at one of them. The eastern side — Sawangan, Melasti, Ungasan's southern edge — is cheaper, calmer and largely overlooked.

   What it is

  Sawangan   sits below Nusa Dua's southern edge, with a long white sand beach, several large resort properties and residential land on the slopes above.

  Melasti   is a dramatic beach reached down a cut through the limestone cliff, with calm turquoise water, beach clubs and a rapidly developing strip above it.

Both face east and southeast, which means   sunrise rather than sunset  , calmer water, and a different swell exposure from the famous western breaks.

   How it differs from the western Bukit

  Calmer water.   Melasti and Sawangan are swimmable in a way Uluwatu, Padang Padang and Bingin frequently are not. For families that is the whole difference.

  White sand  , against the west's mix.

  No surf culture.   The western Bukit's economy runs on waves and the loyal, repeat, direct booking surf market that comes with them. The east does not have that, and it does not have the counter seasonal calendar it produces.

  Cheaper land  , meaningfully, than western clifftop positions.

  Resort presence  , which anchors the area's positioning and brings a different guest.

  Closer to the airport   than Uluwatu, and much closer than Canggu.

   The market

Land on the eastern Bukit is cheaper than the western clifftops and there is more of it, with generous plots and long available lease terms.

Development has accelerated around Melasti as the beach's profile has grown, and prices have moved accordingly. It is no longer undiscovered and it is not yet expensive.

This is largely a land and build market — finished villa stock of the kind foreign buyers want is limited.

   Rental performance

Growing, family weighted, and less seasonal than the western Bukit.

The guest is a family or a couple wanting calm swimmable water, space and a beach club within reach. Tha

t: What documents should a Bali property owner keep?
s: There is no register behind a leasehold. The file you keep is the evidence, and an heir who cannot find it has a genuine problem.
b:
In a registered system, losing your paperwork is inconvenient. In Bali, where   Hak Sewa is not registered anywhere  , the deed in your possession is a substantial part of the evidence that you hold anything at all.

   Why it matters more here

A leasehold appears on no certificate and in no land office record. Your position rests on the notarial deed and the notary's record of it.

A buyer years from now will ask for the file. So will your heirs, so will a tax adviser, and so will anyone resolving a dispute.

  A seller who can produce a complete file transacts faster and at a better price   than one who cannot, and assembling it years later is genuinely difficult.

   The purchase file

  The original deed   — the lease, or the AJB on a registered transfer — with the notary, and a certified copy with you.

  The sworn translation   of anything you signed.

  The land certificate   or a certified copy, depending on the structure.

  The due diligence report   your notary produced.

  Evidence of payment   — transfer confirmations from your own account, showing what was paid and when.

  Tax evidence  : BPHTB payment on a titled transfer, and the seller's disposal tax where relevant.

  The notary's name and contact details  , which is the item most often missing when someone else needs to act.

   The building file

  PBG  , the building approval.

  SLF  , the certificate of fitness.

  As built drawings  , showing what was actually constructed including anything that changed during the build.

  Service locations   — where water lines, electrical runs and drainage actually go. You will need this the first time something fails and reconstructing it later is expensive.

  Warranties   for equipment, waterproofing and structure, with terms and durations.

  Manuals and certificates   for pumps, filtration, aircon, water heating and solar.

  The defects list   from handover, and evidence it was cleared before retention was released.

  Contractor and architect cont

t: Should a Bali villa have its own booking website?
s: Platform commission is fifteen to twenty percent of every booking. A returning guest who books direct is pure margin, and most owners never ask them to.
b:
Airbnb and Booking.com take fifteen to twenty percent between commission and fees. On a villa grossing USD 70,000, that is USD 10,000 to USD 14,000 a year leaving the property for something you could partly do yourself.

   Where direct bookings actually come from

Not from a website ranking in Google. That is the fantasy version and it does not happen for a single villa.

Direct bookings come from   guests who already stayed with you  .

Bali has a much higher repeat rate than most markets, particularly in the surf areas and Ubud, where people return to a break or a programme annually. Those guests already know the property, already trust it, and are the cheapest bookings available to you.

The mechanism is simple and almost nobody does it:   capture the email, and contact them ahead of the season they visited last year.  

   The sequence that works

  During the stay  , provide a genuine reason to share contact details — a local guide you wrote, a restaurant list, a surf forecast tip, the wifi details sent by email.

  At checkout  , thank them and mention that returning guests book direct at a better rate.

  Ten to eleven months later  , one message: we have your dates from last year open, here is the direct rate.

That one message, sent annually to past guests, converts at a rate that makes it the highest return marketing available to a villa owner. It costs nothing.

   What you actually need

  A simple website.   One page, good photographs, the same ones from your listing, a description, a rate table and a way to enquire. It exists to be somewhere to send people, not to be found.

  A booking mechanism.   A form and an email reply is adequate at low volume. A proper booking engine with a calendar is better once you have volume, and inexpensive.

  A calendar that syncs.   This is the one technical thing that matters. Your platform calendars and your direct calendar must stay in sync or you will double book, and a double booking in peak season is a serious p

t: Is Bali airport fast track worth it?
s: A paid service that moves you through immigration and baggage faster. Useful at the wrong hour, irrelevant at the right one.
b:
Ngurah Rai operates close to its designed capacity at peak times, and the queues reflect it. There is a paid way around them.

   What the services do

  Fast track immigration.   An escort meets you at the aircraft door or in the terminal and takes you through a priority immigration lane, bypassing the main queue.

  Baggage assistance  , where a porter collects your bags while you clear immigration.

  Departure assistance  , through check in, immigration and security.

  Full VIP handling  , with a separate lounge, private processing and a vehicle to or from the aircraft, at a considerably higher price.

Offered by the airport's own service and by a number of established private operators.

   When it is genuinely worth it

  Peak arrival windows.   The terminal receives a large number of wide body arrivals in concentrated bands, and immigration queues at those times can run to well over an hour. Fast track turns that into minutes.

  With small children  , after a long flight. This is the case where people who would never otherwise pay for it are glad they did.

  With elderly or mobility limited travellers  , where standing in a long queue is not a minor inconvenience.

  Tight connections  , domestic or international.

  Business arrivals   where time genuinely has a value.

  First trip for guests   you are hosting, if you want the experience to start well.

   When it is not

  Off peak arrivals  , when the hall is quiet and you will clear in fifteen minutes anyway.

  Departures  , generally, where the time saving is smaller and the process is less painful.

  If you already have e VOA  , which removes the payment queue and is free to arrange in advance through the   official immigration portal  . A great deal of what fast track saves is the queue that e VOA already skips.

   Book through the right channel

There is a substantial industry of intermediaries reselling these services at a markup, and a smaller number selling things that do not exist.
