t: How do you protect a Bali villa from guest damage?
s: Most damage is minor and cumulative rather than dramatic. The protection is screening, a deposit, and a written record of condition.
b:
Serious guest damage in Bali villas is rare. Cumulative wear, small breakages and the occasional party that should not have happened are common, and both are manageable with a system.

   What actually goes wrong

  Cumulative wear.   Stains, scratches, chipped tiles, broken glassware, damaged outdoor furniture. Individually trivial, collectively the reason a villa looks tired in three years rather than six.

  Pool and water damage.   Guests who put the wrong things in the pool, or leave taps running, or flood a bathroom.

  Parties.   The genuine risk. A villa booked by four people that hosts forty is where real damage, noise complaints and neighbour problems come from, and it is the scenario worth screening for.

  Smoking indoors  , which in a tropical villa with soft furnishings is expensive to remediate.

  Air conditioning abuse  , running with doors open, which is a cost rather than damage but shows on the bill.

   Screening

  Read the guest profile and reviews.   Platforms show previous host reviews. A guest with no reviews is not disqualifying; a guest with a history of complaints is.

  Ask about the trip.   A short message asking who is coming and what brings them to Bali is normal hospitality and it tells you a great deal. Evasive answers about group size are the signal.

  Watch for the local one night booking.   A local booking for one or two nights at short notice, for a large villa, is the classic party profile. Many Bali owners simply decline these, and a minimum stay of three nights removes most of the problem automatically.

  Minimum stay settings   do more screening work than anything else. Parties book one night; holidays book five.

  Be explicit in the listing.   No parties, maximum occupancy stated, quiet hours. A guest who reads that and books anyway has been told.

   The damage deposit

  Platforms handle this differently   and the mechanisms change, so check the current position for each one. Broadly, platforms offer some form of host

t: Is Medewi or Balian worth buying?
s: Long left-hand waves, almost no development and the cheapest surf-adjacent land in Bali. The rental market is a decade behind.
b:
Past Tabanan, the west coast keeps going for another two hours, and almost nobody buys there. The waves are the reason anyone does.

   What they are

  Balian  , in Tabanan regency, sits where a river meets the sea, with a consistent beach and river mouth break, black sand, and a small cluster of surf accommodation.

  Medewi  , further west in   Jembrana   regency, has one of the longest left hand point waves in Indonesia — a slow, rideable wall that breaks over rounded stones and can run for several hundred metres.

Both are surrounded by rice fields, coconut plantations and working villages, with almost no tourism infrastructure beyond a handful of surf camps, warungs and small guesthouses.

Medewi is roughly   two to two and a half hours from the airport  . Balian is around ninety minutes.

   Why anyone buys

  The wave.   Medewi's left is genuinely world class for the kind of surfing it offers, and it is uncrowded compared to anything in the south. Balian is consistent and serves a similar market.

  Land is the cheapest surf adjacent land in Bali  , by a wide margin, with beachfront positions unobtainable at the price anywhere south.

  Genuine quiet  , in a way the south has entirely lost.

  Scarcity of good waves  , which does not increase.

   Why almost nobody does

  Distance.   Two hours from the airport removes the property from the mainstream rental market entirely. A guest on a week in Bali does not drive two hours each way.

  No infrastructure.   No walkable amenity, no restaurant scene, no coworking, no international schools, no hospital of consequence. Medical care is limited and serious cases travel.

  A very thin rental market.   The demand is surf travellers and a small quiet seeking segment, and both are small in absolute numbers. Occupancy that would be a failure in Canggu is normal here.

  Almost no resale market.   A sale can take years, and on a leasehold the term runs down throughout.

  Two regencies.   Balian is Tabanan, Medewi is

t: Can you buy Bali property without visiting?
s: It is possible and it removes the checks that matter most. If you must do it, this is the structure that makes it survivable.
b:
People buy Bali property without setting foot on it, and some of them do fine. The ones who do not are almost always the ones who skipped the same three things.

   What visiting actually gives you

  The street at different times.   Noise from a bar, a junction, a mosque or a construction site. Traffic at the hour guests actually travel. What the area is like on a Tuesday rather than in a photograph.

  The neighbours  , and what they might build. A rice field or ocean view over land somebody else owns is not protected, and standing there is how you understand what is at risk.

  The condition.   Water pressure at the highest point. Whether the pool holds water overnight. Whether there is a smell near the septic soakaway. Damp, mould, cracks, termite evidence.

  The drive.   From the airport, at the hour a guest lands. From the property to the beach, to a restaurant, to anything.

  The feel  , which is not a small thing. Plenty of people have bought a property that was correct on paper and wrong for them.

None of that is available through a screen.

   If you are buying remotely anyway

  Engage your own notary  , not one introduced by the agent. This is the only independent check in the transaction and it matters more, not less, when you are not present.

  Engage an independent surveyor   to inspect the building and walk the boundary against the certificate. A few hundred dollars, and they are your eyes. Instruct them directly and pay them directly.

  Commission your own photographs and video  , taken by someone you engaged, including the things a seller would not photograph — the access road, the neighbours, the equipment housing, the septic area, the ceiling in every room.

  Get someone to visit at different times   and report. Early morning, evening, after rain.

  Verify everything documentary  : certificate at the land office, seller's entitlement, zoning for the exact parcel, PBG and SLF against the building, encumbrances, existing leases and managemen

t: Second home visa or golden visa for Indonesia?
s: Two long-stay routes based on funds rather than employment, with different qualifying bases and both newer than the alternatives in the region.
b:
Indonesia has two headline routes for people who want to live here without a job, a business role or an Indonesian spouse. They are frequently confused and they work differently.

   The second home route

Designed for foreign nationals who want to reside in Indonesia for an extended period, qualifying on   funds held   — typically a deposit in an Indonesian state bank at a defined threshold — or on ownership of property above a defined value.

The emphasis is on   demonstrated financial capacity   rather than on an investment being deployed into a business.

   The golden visa framework

Broader, with   several categories  :

  Investment based  , where capital is committed into an Indonesian company or into government instruments at defined thresholds, with different durations attached to different levels.

  Talent based  , for foreign nationals whose qualifications, expertise or record are considered to bring value — researchers, academics, recognised professionals, founders. The basis is your record rather than a sum of money.

  Corporate categories  , where a company sponsors executives.

  Family categories  , extending to dependants of a principal holder.

  Other designations  , including routes aimed at older applicants and at former Indonesian citizens and their descendants.

   The practical difference

  Second home   is about having funds and wanting to live here.

  Golden visa investment categories   are about deploying capital into Indonesia.

  Golden visa talent categories   are about who you are professionally.

If you have savings and want to retire or semi retire here, the second home route is the one aimed at you. If you are committing capital to an Indonesian business, the investment categories are. If you have professional standing and do not want to commit capital, the talent route is.

   What neither of them does

  Neither is work authorisation.  

This is the point people get wrong across every Indonesian long stay route. Holding one d

t: What visit visa types exist for Indonesia?
s: Short courses, work trials, conferences and exhibitions each have a visit visa category. The line between attending and working is what matters.
b:
Indonesia has more visit visa categories than most people realise, aimed at specific short term purposes. They matter because the alternative — using a tourist visa for something it does not cover — is the exposure.

   The categories

  Short course or training.   Attending a course, a training programme or a certification, at a recognised provider. Common in Bali for yoga teacher training, diving certification, language study and professional courses.

  Work trial or probation.   Where a company is assessing a foreign candidate before committing to an employment arrangement, within defined limits.

  Event participation.   Conferences, exhibitions, trade fairs, seminars — attending, exhibiting or speaking.

  Business visit.   Meetings, negotiations, site visits and due diligence.

  Sports and competition.   Participating in events.

  Filming and journalism  , which have their own requirements and are more tightly controlled than people assume.

Index codes and requirements   change  , so verify the current category and its conditions rather than following an older list.

   The line that decides everything

  Attending, learning, observing, discussing and assessing   are visit activities.

  Producing, delivering, teaching, performing and directing   are work.

  Payment is not the test.   Indonesian immigration practice treats productive activity as work regardless of whether you receive anything.

So: attending a yoga teacher training is a visit activity. Teaching on one is work. Attending a conference is a visit activity. Speaking at it commercially, running a workshop, or exhibiting and selling is closer to work and may need different authorisation.

The distinction sounds fine and it is the one that gets enforced.

   Short courses specifically

Bali's course economy is large — yoga, diving, surfing, language, wellness, culinary.

  Attending   a course at a recognised provider is straightforward and there is a category for it where a stay exceeds what a

t: Is Tibubeneng or Padonan worth buying?
s: The residential belt behind Berawa, cheaper than the coast and close enough to use it, with zoning as the main thing to verify.
b:
Tibubeneng and Padonan sit immediately inland from Berawa and the Canggu Shortcut, and they are where the corridor's overflow has gone.

   What they are

  Tibubeneng   is the administrative village covering much of the Canggu area, extending inland from Berawa toward the shortcut and Kerobokan. Parts of it are dense and developed; parts remain rice fields.

  Padonan   sits further inland, more residential and more local in character, with villa development scattered among family housing and agricultural land.

Five to fifteen minutes from Berawa's amenity, ten to twenty from Batu Bolong, depending on traffic — which on the shortcut is significant.

No beach, no walkable strip. You drive or ride for everything.

   The market

Land is   meaningfully cheaper than Berawa or Batu Bolong  , and there is more of it, with larger plots and lease terms that run longer at the same budget.

This is the practical answer for buyers who want to be in the Canggu catchment and cannot pay coastal prices.

Stock is a mix of newer villa development and older local housing. Both buying and building are viable, unlike the coastal strip where land barely trades.

   Rental performance

Moderate, and it depends entirely on what you build.

  Short term nightly letting   underperforms the coastal strip. Guests booking a Canggu holiday want walkability or a beach, and these areas offer neither. Rates and occupancy sit below Berawa for an equivalent property.

  Long term and monthly rental is strong.   Residents, people working in Bali, families and long stay remote workers who want space and a pool without coastal prices. Demand is steady, year round and much less seasonal than the tourist market.

The honest position is that this is a   long term rental area that some owners try to run as a short term one  . Run it as what it is and the numbers work well — lower gross, much lower operating cost and workload, and a calendar that does not collapse in February.

t: Can you host weddings and events at a Bali villa?
s: Events pay several times a normal night and carry licensing, neighbour and community consequences that a nightly booking does not.
b:
A wedding at a Bali villa can generate more revenue in two days than a fortnight of ordinary bookings. It also introduces a set of issues that nightly letting does not, and the ones that matter most are not commercial.

   The commercial case

  Rates are high.   Event hire is priced well above nightly accommodation, and a wedding typically books the villa for several days around the event.

  Bali is a genuine wedding destination  , particularly for Australian and Asian regional couples, with an established supplier ecosystem — planners, caterers, florists, photographers, celebrants.

  It fills shoulder season  , because weddings are planned around availability and price rather than around school holidays, and they book far ahead.

  Repeat and referral   are strong. Guests at a good wedding become guests.

   The licensing question

This is where it gets complicated and where most operators are not where they think they are.

  Accommodation and events are different activities.   A villa licensed for accommodation — where that licensing exists at all — is not automatically permitted to operate as an event venue.

Commercial event hosting may engage   separate licensing  , and the   KBLI classification   of the operating entity determines what it may lawfully do. A company classified for accommodation is not classified for event management.

  Bali closed new foreign owned villa and homestay registration to PMA companies on 22 July 2026  , which affects the underlying accommodation position for foreign investors before you even reach the event question.

  Serving alcohol   at an event is a licensed activity in its own right, tiered by beverage category and tied to specific premises.

Confirm the position for your property and your entity specifically, with a local adviser, before marketing the villa for events. "Other villas do it" is not a licence.

   The neighbours, which matter more

This is the part that decides whether events work at your property long term

t: What permit can the parent of an Indonesian citizen get?
s: Family connection to an Indonesian citizen opens routes that are not available to unconnected foreign nationals.
b:
Indonesia recognises family connection as a basis for residency, and the routes reach further than most people expect.

   Who can sponsor

  An Indonesian citizen   can sponsor certain foreign family members for stay permits, and the category depends on the relationship.

  A KITAS or KITAP holder   can sponsor a spouse and children as dependants.

The strongest position is connection to an   Indonesian citizen  , because it does not depend on someone else's permit continuing.

   The relationships that qualify

  A foreign spouse   of an Indonesian citizen, which is the most common and most established route, leading in time toward KITAP.

  Foreign children   of an Indonesian citizen — though where the child was born to a mixed marriage, the more important question is usually the   dual citizenship   position rather than a permit, because an Indonesian citizen child can hold Hak Milik freehold and a foreign one cannot.

  Foreign parents of an Indonesian citizen.   This is the one people do not know about. Where an adult Indonesian citizen has a foreign parent — through a mixed marriage, through a parent who naturalised elsewhere, or through adoption — there is a basis for the parent to obtain residency sponsored by the child.

  Stepchildren and adopted children  , with their own requirements and documentation.

Specific categories, index codes and conditions change. Verify the current position for the actual relationship rather than assuming from a general description.

   The documents, which are the bottleneck

Every one of these depends on   evidencing the relationship  , and that is where applications stall.

  Birth certificates, marriage certificates, adoption orders, naturalisation records.  

  Where documents were issued abroad  , they need   legalisation   — by apostille, since Indonesia is a party to the Hague Convention — and   sworn translation   by a  penerjemah tersumpah .

t: Berawa or Batu Bolong?
s: A kilometre apart and genuinely different markets. Batu Bolong sells walkability, Berawa sells amenity and space.
b:
These two sit a kilometre apart and buyers treat them as interchangeable. They are not, and the difference determines what you should build and who books it.

   Batu Bolong

  The most walkable stretch in Canggu  , and that is the entire product.

A guest can leave the villa on foot, reach breakfast, the beach, dinner and home. In Bali that is close to unique, and it is what the land price reflects.

  The wave   is a beginner to intermediate beach break with surf schools along the sand.

  The guest   skews to couples, digital nomads on monthly stays and surf travellers, with a strong repeat market. That nomad population is what fills February and March, which is where the annual number is decided.

  The constraint is plot size.   Land is the most expensive per are in Canggu and the plots are small. Combined with KDB coverage limits, fitting a villa with a pool that photographs well is genuinely difficult, and a lot of newer stock sacrificed outdoor space for bedrooms.

  Lease terms available at a given budget are the shortest in the corridor  , because the land underneath is the most expensive.

   Berawa

  Amenity and space  , rather than walkability.

The strip carries Atlas, Finns, La Brisa and a continuous run of restaurants, gyms, clinics and co working. It has the infrastructure of a small town.

  Plots are larger   and the area is less tightly built than Batu Bolong, which means four and five bedroom villas with proper pools and gardens are deliverable here in a way they are not a kilometre south.

  The guest mix is the broadest in Bali   — families, groups, couples, nomads, Australians, Europeans. That breadth produces the steadiest occupancy on the island.

  The deepest resale market in Canggu  , which on a leasehold is worth real money.

  The constraint is congestion.   The Berawa road is busy most of the day, parking is difficult, and drainage is a recurring wet season issue on several streets.

t: Does land banking work in Bali?
s: Buying land and waiting works when the land appreciates faster than a lease term decays. On a leasehold, it usually does not.
b:
Buying land in an emerging corridor and holding it while the area develops is the most intuitive Bali strategy there is. It also contains a structural problem most people buying into it have not noticed.

   The intuitive version

Seminyak filled, so Canggu developed. Canggu filled, so Pererenan. Then Cemagi, Seseh, Kedungu, and now into Tabanan.

That movement has been reliable for two decades. Buy one corridor ahead of the wave, wait, sell into the wave.

People have done very well doing exactly this.

   The problem with doing it on a leasehold

  A leasehold does not capture land appreciation.  

You do not own the land. You hold a defined number of years of use over it, and that number goes down every year.

So while the land underneath appreciates — to the landowner's benefit — your asset is decaying. A thirty year lease over land worth USD 300,000 loses roughly USD 10,000 a year to the running term, and land appreciation does not offset it because the appreciation is not yours.

At the end you hand back land worth three times what it was, and you have nothing.

  Land banking on a leasehold is holding a wasting asset while someone else's asset appreciates.   That is not a land bank. It is a long, expensive option that expires worthless.

   When it does work on a leasehold

Only if you   sell the remaining lease   into a stronger market, at a price reflecting both the improved area and the term remaining.

That can work, and it requires two things: a genuinely long initial term, so there is enough remaining to be worth buying when you sell, and an area that develops fast enough to move prices before the decay eats the gain.

A thirty year lease sold in year eight into a corridor that has repriced is a real trade. A twenty year lease sold in year twelve is a difficult sale at any price.

The discipline:   buy the longest term available, and plan to exit early in it, not late.  

   The structures that do capture appreciation

t: Which platforms should a Bali villa list on?
s: More listings means more exposure and one calendar to keep in sync. Getting that wrong in August is the most expensive administrative error available.
b:
Listing on more platforms increases exposure and introduces one technical problem that has to be solved before you do it.

   The platforms that matter here

  Airbnb   is the largest source of villa bookings in Bali, particularly for the Australian, European and nomad segments, and particularly for longer stays.

  Booking.com   brings a different guest — often shorter stays, more Asian regional traffic, and travellers who book accommodation the way they book hotels.

  Agoda   has genuine strength in Asian regional markets and is underused by foreign villa owners.

  Specialist Bali villa sites   and local agencies reach an audience that goes looking specifically for a villa rather than browsing a global platform.

  Direct  , which is where repeat guests should end up.

Each reaches a different person. A villa on one platform is visible to a fraction of the market.

   Commission

Fifteen to twenty percent between commission and fees on the major platforms, with structures differing between them and changing periodically.

That is the price of acquisition, and for new guests it is generally worth paying. The mistake is paying it repeatedly for the same guest.

   The double booking problem

This is the technical issue and it is not optional.

If you list on three platforms with three separate calendars, a booking on one does not block the others. In February that is a minor inconvenience.   In August it means two groups arriving at the same villa on the same day  , and one of them has flown from Perth.

The consequences are a cancellation, a refund, a very bad review, and on some platforms a penalty affecting your ranking.

   How to prevent it

  iCal synchronisation   is the free option. Platforms publish and subscribe to calendar feeds, and they block each other's dates.

It works and it is not instantaneous. Feeds update periodically rather than in real time, which leaves a window where two bookings can land. On a low volume property that window rarely bites.

t: What happens if you move address in Indonesia?
s: Systems match data strictly and reject rather than query. An address updated in one place and not another produces a failure at the worst moment.
b:
Moving house in Indonesia generates administrative work in several places, and skipping it produces a failure months later in a process you cared about.

   Where your address is recorded

  Your stay permit record   with immigration.

  Your SKTT   — the certificate of residence issued by the civil registry to a KITAS holder.

  Your tax registration  , the NPWP.

  Your bank  , which used the address for its own verification.

  Your company's registered address  , if you have one, in the deed, the NIB and the OSS record.

  Utility and service accounts.  

These are separate systems. Updating one does not update the others.

   Why it matters more than it sounds

Indonesian administration now runs through platforms that   match data strictly and reject rather than query  .

  Coretax  , the tax administration system, fails a filing where a name or address does not reconcile. It does not telephone you.

  Immigration   surfaces an inconsistency at a KITAS extension, which is exactly when you have no time to fix it.

  Banks   reject applications on mismatches rather than asking about them.

So an address updated with immigration but not with the civil registry, or updated in both but not on the tax record, is an inconsistency sitting there waiting for the moment you need something.

   When it bites

  At a KITAS extension  , where the address on the permit does not match the SKTT.

  At a tax filing  , where Coretax rejects on a data mismatch.

  At a bank  , opening an account or making a large transfer, where proof of address does not match the record.

  At a licence renewal  , if the company's registered address is stale.

  At a property transaction  , where identity documents have to reconcile.

  At a driving licence application  , which requires current proof of residence.

   What to update, in order

  The civil registry (Dukcapil)   for your   SKTT  , which is the document most other things rely on as proof of address.

  Immigration  , to reflect the

t: What does a Bali villa pool cost to run?
s: The pool is the product. It is also a daily chemistry problem in a tropical climate and the most visible thing that goes wrong.
b:
In a Bali villa the pool is not an amenity, it is the product. It is the cover image, it is why the booking happened, and it is the thing guests photograph. It is also the item most likely to be visibly wrong.

   What it costs to run

  A pool service   — two to three visits a week, chemicals, brushing, skimming, filter cleaning — is an ordinary monthly cost and modest relative to the rest of the operation. Most villas contract it rather than employing someone directly.

  Electricity for the pump   is the larger ongoing number and it is frequently overlooked. A pump running an unnecessarily long daily cycle is a meaningful share of a villa's power bill.

  Water  , for topping up. Evaporation in this climate is substantial, and on the Bukit where water is trucked, pool top up is a genuine cost that scales with sun and occupancy.

  Chemicals  , continuously, because the tropical combination of heat, sun, rain and bathers is hard on water balance.

  Periodic resurfacing  , which is the capital item. Pool surfaces have a finite life and resurfacing is a several thousand dollar job that takes the pool — and effectively the villa — out of service for a period.

   Why it is harder here

  Heat and sun   accelerate chlorine loss, which means more chemical and tighter management.

  Rain   dilutes and unbalances the water, and a heavy wet season downpour changes the chemistry in an afternoon.

  Organic load.   Leaves, frangipani flowers, insects and whatever the garden drops. A pool sited under heavy planting is a permanent cleaning problem, which is why what you plant near it matters.

  Occupancy spikes.   Ten people in a pool for a week is a very different load from two.

  Algae   establishes fast in warm water and a pool that goes wrong on a Friday looks green by Sunday.

   The failures that cost you

  Green water on arrival.   The single worst guest experience a Bali villa can deliver, because the pool is the reason they booked. It produces a refund conversati

t: How do you fix an underperforming Bali villa?
s: Most underperforming villas are not bad properties. They are averagely run, and the fixes are cheap and in a specific order.
b:
A villa running at fifty five percent occupancy in a street where comparable properties run at seventy five is not a bad villa. It is a villa with three or four fixable problems, and they are almost always the same ones.

   First, find out if there is actually a problem

  Compare properly.   Watch four or five genuinely comparable villas — same street, same bedroom count, same price band — and track their availability calendars over six to eight weeks. Record which dates fill and at what price.

That tells you what a property like yours actually achieves. Your monthly statement tells you what happened; the comparison tells you what should have.

If you are within a few points of comparable properties, the property is fine and the market is what it is. If you are twenty points below, keep reading.

   The order to fix things

This is deliberate. Doing it in a different order wastes money.

  One: photography.   The cheapest and highest return fix available, and the one most owners have never redone. A guest decides in about a second on one image against fifty alternatives. Professional photography, shot in early morning or the hour before sunset, with the pool leading and an evening shot included, routinely moves bookings twenty to thirty percent on the same property.

  Two: the listing order.   Free. Most listings bury the best image at position nine. The first five carry almost all the weight: pool with villa, main living space, best bedroom, evening or drone shot, bathroom. Reorder it this afternoon.

  Three: pricing.   One annual rate is the most common error. Bali has four genuine seasons, and the annual number is decided in February, March and November, not August. Set seasonal bands, check your floor — the rate below which a booking costs you money — and use monthly rates through the trough.

  Four: response time and reviews.   Platform ranking rewards both. A manager responding in hours rather than minutes is costing you visibility.

  Five: the garden.

t: What is the difference between an agent and a manager in Bali?
s: An agent sells and is paid on the transaction. A manager operates and is paid on revenue. Neither is your adviser unless you engaged them as one.
b:
Bali's property ecosystem has several roles that look similar from outside and have entirely different incentives. Knowing who is paid for what is the most useful thing you can understand about the market.

   The agent

  Paid a commission on a completed sale  , normally by the seller, at three to five percent.

  Works for the seller.   Almost always, even when they found the property for you, showed it to you and answered your questions helpfully.

  Not licensed.   There is no licensing regime for real estate agents in Indonesia — no professional standards body, no mandatory disclosure, no indemnity regime.

That does not make agents dishonest. Most are not. It means   the questions you do not ask do not get answered  , and that nobody in the room is working solely for you unless you engaged them.

  What to do:   use agents to find property, and verify everything independently. Ask directly who they act for and how they are paid. And never accept the notary they introduce.

   The notary

  The only genuinely independent check available to you  , and only if you engaged them.

A notary introduced by the agent has an ongoing commercial relationship with someone paid on the sale. Engaging your own costs a little more and it is the single most important decision in the transaction.

   The property manager

  Paid a percentage of gross revenue  , fifteen to twenty five percent, sometimes with fixed fees on top or a markup on maintenance.

  Incentive:   revenue, which is broadly aligned with yours. The misalignment is in   effort   — a manager earns more from an extra booking and considerably more from an easier life across a portfolio, and the marginal booking on your property is the one that gets dropped first.

That is the mechanism behind the most common failure in Bali: a manager who performs adequately at first and quietly drifts, while nobody tells the owner.

  What to do:   compare your achieved rate and occupancy against four comparable villas each quart

t: What makes a Bali villa guest experience good?
s: Reviews drive ranking and rate. The things that move them are cheap, specific and mostly decided before the guest arrives.
b:
Reviews drive platform ranking, ranking drives visibility, visibility drives occupancy and occupancy drives your return. That chain starts with things that cost almost nothing.

   What reviews actually punish

In rough order of frequency in Bali:

  Aircon that does not cool.   Usually an undersized unit or a dirty filter. Both avoidable.

  Slow or unreliable internet  , which for the remote worker segment that fills February and March is the whole booking.

  The pool not being right.   Green, cloudy, or not clean on arrival. The pool is the product and this is the worst thing that can go wrong.

  Slow response   when something breaks.

  Noise   — a road, a bar, a construction site, roosters. Some of it is unfixable and all of it should be disclosed.

  A listing that overstated something.   "Ten minutes from Canggu" when it is thirty five at the times guests travel. Mismatch between expectation and reality produces worse reviews than a modest property honestly described.

  Mosquitoes.  

  A bad mattress  , which is one of the cheapest things to get right.

   What reviews reward

  Being met.   Someone there on arrival, with a cold drink, who shows them the villa. This costs nothing and it appears in reviews constantly.

  Responsiveness.   Problems get solved fast. Guests forgive faults and do not forgive being ignored.

  Anticipation.   The thing they needed before they asked.

  Local knowledge.   A genuinely useful guide to the area — where to eat that is not on every list, where the good waves are for their level, which beach is calm for children.

  Cleanliness  , to a standard above what the rate suggests.

   The welcome pack

Physical or digital, and it does disproportionate work.

  Wifi details  , prominently, because it is the first thing every guest looks for.

  How everything works   — aircon, pool, safe, hot water, the gate.

  Who to call  , with a name and a number that answers.

t: Should you sell a Bali villa furnished?
s: Furniture is worth more inside a photograph than outside one. Selling empty costs you the images that sell the property.
b:
Most Bali villas sell furnished, and the owners who strip them first usually wish they had not.

   Why furnished sells better

  Empty villas photograph badly.   They read smaller, they look unfinished and they give a buyer nothing to react to. A furnished villa in good photographs sells on the images; an empty one has to sell on the floor plan.

  Buyers are frequently investors  , and an investor wants an asset that can take a guest next month. A furnished villa with an existing listing is a business. An empty one is a project with a USD 25,000 to USD 50,000 fit out bill and three months before it earns.

  Furniture here is worth little on resale   and a great deal in place. Used pieces from a humid climate have a thin secondhand market, and the cost of storing, moving and selling them usually exceeds what they fetch.

  It removes a negotiation.   A sale where furniture is separately valued and argued over is a sale with an extra way to stall.

   What "furnished" should actually mean

Be specific in the agreement, because ambiguity here causes disputes at handover.

  An inventory  , itemised and photographed, attached to the contract. What stays, what goes.

  Personal effects excluded   explicitly.

  Anything you intend to remove named  , so it is not discovered missing on the final walkthrough.

  Consumables and linen   addressed — a buyer taking over an operating villa expects the towels and sheets that were in the photographs.

  Equipment  : pool gear, garden tools, maintenance items, spare parts. These are worth almost nothing and their absence is immediately annoying.

   When to sell empty

  If the furniture is genuinely tired.   Worn pieces make a good property look neglected, and a buyer mentally deducts the replacement cost anyway.

In that case, either refresh it before listing — paint, soft furnishings, styling, then rephotograph — or clear it and present a clean empty space rather than a shabby furnished one.

t: Does a Bali villa need a name and a brand?
s: A name is free and it is the only part of your listing a guest remembers. Most owners choose one badly and never think about it again.
b:
Every Bali villa has a name and almost none of them were chosen deliberately. It is the cheapest piece of positioning available and it does more work than owners expect.

   What a name actually does

  It is what a returning guest searches for.   A guest who stayed two years ago and wants to book again types a name into Google. If yours is "Villa Sunrise" — one of several hundred — they will not find you, and that repeat booking goes to a platform instead of direct.

  It is what a guest tells a friend.   Word of mouth is a real channel in Bali, and it runs on names.

  It is your direct booking asset.   A distinctive name that ranks for itself is the foundation of every direct booking you will ever take, and direct bookings save the fifteen to twenty percent platform commission.

  It sets an expectation   before anyone reads a word of the listing.

   What makes a bad villa name in Bali

  Generic tropical words.   Sunrise, Serenity, Paradise, Bliss, Harmony, Zen, Lotus. All used hundreds of times, none searchable, none memorable.

  "Villa" plus a common Indonesian word  , which describes half the island's stock.

  Anything hard to spell   from hearing it, which breaks the word of mouth chain.

  Anything that means something unintended   in Indonesian or Balinese. Check with a local speaker before committing to signage.

  A name tied to a feature that might change  , like the view or a tree.

   What makes a good one

  Distinctive enough to be searchable.   Type your candidate into Google with "Bali" and see what comes back. If it returns four hundred other villas, choose again.

  Short and spellable.   Two words, easy to say once and repeat.

  Connected to something real   — the street, the village, a local landmark, a genuine feature of the property, a word with actual meaning.

  Consistent with the property.   A name implying luxury on a modest two bedroom sets an expectation you will fail.

  Available.   Check the domain, check the platform listings,

t: How should a Bali villa be cleaned between guests?
s: Cleanliness is the review category most likely to be marked down and the cheapest to get right. The climate makes it harder than at home.
b:
Cleanliness is the single most consistently reviewed thing about a villa, it is the cheapest category to score well in, and Bali's climate makes it considerably harder than the equivalent property at home.

   Why it is harder here

  Humidity produces mould  , continuously, in wardrobes, on ceilings, behind furniture and in anything that does not dry. Cleaning it off is not the same as preventing it, and it comes back.

  Insects.   Ants find anything, geckos leave droppings, and mosquitoes are what guests actually mention.

  Open buildings.   Bali villas are designed to let air through, which also lets in dust, leaves and everything else.

  The garden grows constantly   and drops into the pool and onto terraces.

  Salt near the coast   corrodes fittings and marks surfaces.

A villa cleaned to a home standard once a week will not present well. It needs a schedule built for the environment.

   The turnover standard

  Every surface  , including the ones guests do not see, because what is behind a door is what a guest opens.

  Bathrooms properly   — grout, drains, behind the toilet, the shower screen. Bathrooms are what guests judge and what reviews mention.

  Linen changed and properly dried.   Damp smelling linen in a humid climate is the most common complaint in this category and it comes from inadequate drying rather than inadequate washing.   Three sets per bed   is the working figure so nothing is rushed.

  Kitchen  , including inside the fridge, the kettle, the coffee equipment and the cupboards.

  Outdoor areas  : terrace swept, furniture wiped, cushions dry and not mouldy, pool deck clean.

  Pool   clean and clear, which is separate from housekeeping and should be verified at the same time.

  Aircon filters  , on a schedule. Dirty filters reduce output and produce the "aircon didn't work" review.

  Restocking  : consumables, toilet paper, water, basics.

   The weekly and monthly layer

Turnover cleaning is not enough on its own.

  Weekly  : deep

t: Should you buy a second property in Bali?
s: The second one is easier than the first and the economics only improve at three or four. Below that you carry the same overhead twice.
b:
The first Bali property teaches you more than any amount of research. The question is whether a second one makes sense, and the answer depends on where the costs actually sit.

   What the second one is easier at

  You know the market.   Street level comparables, what a realistic rate is, what management costs, which areas suit which guest. That knowledge is the most valuable thing the first purchase produced.

  You have the relationships.   A notary you trust, a manager who performs, a contractor, a tax adviser. Rebuilding those is a large part of what makes a first purchase slow and risky.

  You know your own numbers.   Actual operating costs, actual occupancy, actual seasonality for your guest type — not a projection.

  You can see the mistakes.   Most owners can name three things they would do differently, and the second purchase is where they do them.

   Where scale does not help at two

  Management fees stay the same.   Fifteen to twenty five percent of gross on both, unless you negotiate, and a manager with two properties is not meaningfully cheaper per property than one with a single.

  Compliance stays the same.   If you use a PT PMA, the annual load is per company rather than per property — so a second property inside an existing structure adds little, while a second structure doubles it.

  Your attention divides.   Two properties need two quarterly reviews, two sets of comparables, two managers to watch. The work roughly doubles.

  Concentration risk increases.   Two villas in the same corridor is one bet placed twice. An area problem, a regulatory change or a flight capacity event hits both.

At two, you carry most of the overhead twice and capture very little of the scale.

   Where scale actually starts

  Three or four  , and it comes from a small number of places:

  Management leverage.   A manager running four of your properties will negotiate on rate and will prioritise you. That is a real saving and a real improvement in attention.

t: Can you rent out your Bali home when you are away?
s: Using a property yourself and letting it the rest of the year is a common plan with a licensing question and an arithmetic problem.
b:
Buying a home in Bali and letting it while you are away is the most common plan foreign buyers arrive with. It works, and two things about it are consistently underestimated.

   The licensing question

  Letting nightly to paying guests is commercial accommodation  , regardless of the fact that you live there the rest of the year.

That requires zoning that permits it, an operating entity with the correct KBLI classification, PBG and SLF, and operational licensing — noting Bali closed new foreign owned villa and homestay registration to PMA companies on   22 July 2026  .

Plenty of owner occupiers let nightly without all of that. The practical consequence is rarely enforcement; it is that the property becomes   unsaleable to any buyer doing proper due diligence  , and a tax liability accumulates.

  Long term letting to a single tenant sits differently   and does not engage the accommodation framework in the same way, which for some owner occupiers resolves the question entirely.

Confirm your specific position rather than assuming either direction.

   The arithmetic problem

  The weeks you use are the weeks worth the most.  

If you take six weeks in July and August, that is peak — rates forty to seventy percent above base, and a period when a decent property fills at almost any price.

Six peak weeks in a four bedroom is a very large number, and it is income you did not earn. An owner occupier who models a full year yield and then takes the best six weeks has overstated their return substantially.

  Model it honestly.   Take your realistic annual net, subtract the weeks you will actually use at their seasonal rate, and look at what remains. Then decide whether the use is worth it — which it very often is, and it should be a conscious trade rather than an accident.

  If you can be flexible, take shoulder season.   May, June, September and early October are excellent in Bali and cost you far less income than August does.

t: Is a Bali villa safe for children?
s: Family bookings are a large share of the market and the properties that win them are explicit about safety rather than silent.
b:
Families are one of the largest segments in the Bali market, particularly Australian families in school holidays. The properties that attract them are the ones that answer the safety question before it is asked.

   The pool, which is the whole subject

Drowning is the risk that matters, and Bali villa pools are frequently designed without it in mind.

  What helps:  

  Visibility from the living space.   A parent in the kitchen who can see the pool is the single most effective safety feature a villa can have, and it is a design decision rather than a product.

  A clearly defined edge  , and a shallow area where small children can stand.

  Depth markings  , so guests know.

  Good lighting  , for evening.

  Non slip surfaces   around the pool, which matter as much as the water does.

  A gate or fence  , which is the explicit option. It affects photographs, and a meaningful number of families search for it specifically. Whether you install one is a judgement about your market — but   state the position clearly in the listing   either way. A family arriving to discover an unfenced pool they assumed was fenced is a bad outcome for everyone.

  Pool alarms and safety nets   exist and are used by some operators.

   The other risks

  Steps and level changes  , which Bali villas have a great many of, frequently without handrails, and often wet.

  Open sides and balconies  , which are part of the architecture and a hazard with small children. Gaps in balustrades matter.

  Sharp landscaping   — stone edges, decorative features.

  Electrical  , where older installations frequently lack earthing and safety cutouts. This is worth checking regardless of families.

  Hot water  , at a temperature that can scald.

  Mosquitoes  , with dengue present in Bali, which is a genuine health issue rather than a nuisance. Eliminate standing water, provide repellent, consider screens.

  The beach.   Many Bali beaches have strong currents and no lifeguard. If yours is one, say so

t: Is Bali property a good idea for retirees?
s: Cheaper living, a warm climate and a residency route that exists. Against that, a wasting asset, thin liquidity and healthcare with a ceiling.
b:
Bali works well for a lot of retirees and badly for a specific kind of plan. The difference is whether the purchase assumes the property is an asset for your children.

   What works

  Cost of living   is meaningfully lower than Australia, Western Europe or North America, particularly if you live somewhat locally rather than entirely in the foreign economy.

  Domestic help   is affordable in a way it is not at home, which matters more with age than people anticipate.

  Climate  , and a pace of life that suits a lot of people.

  A residency route exists.   The retirement KITAS, the silver hair designation and the second home route are all aimed at older applicants meeting age, income and accommodation conditions.

  Residency makes Hak Pakai available   — a registered right of use over property in your own name at the land office, which is the strongest ownership position open to a foreign individual and unavailable without a KITAS or KITAP.

That last point matters more for retirees than for anyone else, because someone intending to live here permanently is exactly the person who should not be holding a wasting lease.

   What does not

  The leasehold problem.   If you take a thirty year lease at sixty five, it runs out at ninety five, and your heirs inherit nothing unless the deed binds heirs and successors — which many do not.

A foreign heir cannot hold Hak Milik, and inherited freehold is subject to disposal rules.   Plan the inheritance position deliberately  , with an Indonesian will and advice, rather than assuming.

  Healthcare has a ceiling.   Private hospitals in the south handle routine and moderately serious care competently. Major trauma, complex cardiac, serious neurological and advanced oncology cases are generally   evacuated to Singapore or Australia  , at a cost of tens of thousands of dollars.

t: Does the Bali property market have cycles?
s: Four disruptions in twenty-five years, each followed by recovery. An investment that only works in good years has no margin for what this market does.
b:
Bali's property market is usually discussed as though it only goes one way. The record says otherwise, and the pattern matters for how you underwrite.

   What has actually happened

  The 2002 and 2005 bombings.   Tourism collapsed, visitor numbers took years to recover, and property values and rental income fell with them.

  The 2017 to 2019 Agung eruption sequence.   Repeated airport closures as ash drifted across flight paths. No flights means no guests, island wide, regardless of where a property sits. Occupancy collapsed across Bali, not only in the east.

  The pandemic.   Borders closed, the tourism economy stopped almost entirely, and a large number of businesses did not survive it. Owners with debt, staff obligations and no income had a very difficult two years.

  The 2018 Lombok earthquakes  , which caused extensive damage on Lombok and the Gilis and affected sentiment more broadly.

Four significant disruptions in roughly twenty five years. Each was followed by recovery, and each was survivable for owners with margin and difficult for owners without.

   What the recoveries tell you

  Demand came back every time.   The underlying draw — climate, coast, culture, cost — did not change, and visitor numbers returned and exceeded previous peaks.

  Land held value better than income did.   Rental income went to nothing during the closures; land in well zoned coastal locations did not reprice downward to the same degree, because the scarcity did not change.

  Recovery took years, not months  , in each case.

  The market's structure changed afterwards.   Post pandemic Bali has a substantially larger digital nomad population and a different guest mix from 2019, which is why occupancy in Canggu and Pererenan holds through months that would previously have been quiet.
